title: Programmable aliphatic C–H site selection
open: Develop catalysts that functionalize a specified non-equivalent aliphatic C–H bond in a complex molecule while preserving competing sites and sensitive functional groups, without installing a directing group. Establish transferable rules for changing the selected site.
status: A decades-old selectivity problem. In 2025, catalyst redesign switched arylcyclohexane functionalization between C1 and C4; general addressability across molecular scaffolds remains open.
why: Enables medicinal analogue synthesis with fewer protection and reconstruction steps.
key_works: Davies and coworkers (2025), *Impact of Induced Fitting and Secondary Noncovalent Interactions on Site-Selective and Enantioselective C–H Functionalization of Arylcyclohexanes*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c06398](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c06398).

title: Directing-group-free arene site selection
open: Select independently among non-equivalent positions of substituted arenes using catalyst choice, including positions disfavored by substrate electronics and sterics. Extend this control to heteroarenes and multifunctional medicinal scaffolds.
status: Longstanding. Host–guest-controlled borylation in 2026 extended selectivity to substrates lacking conventional recognition groups; broad recognition across molecular shapes remains unresolved.
why: Makes positional-isomer libraries accessible from common starting materials.
key_works: Su, Takeda and Kuninobu (2026), *Host–Guest Interaction-Controlled Site-Selective C–H Borylation of Aromatic Compounds*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c21178](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c21178).

title: Unstrained C–C cleavage at a chosen bond
open: Cleave and replace a selected unstrained C–C bond in a multifunctional molecule without relying on ring-strain release, privileged directing groups or destructive fragmentation elsewhere.
status: A longstanding skeletal-editing challenge. Alkyne-bridged palladium chemistry in 2025 enabled cleavage in unstrained ketones, esters and amides; arbitrary backbone bonds remain substantially less accessible.
why: Allows molecular frameworks to be diversified after their construction.
key_works: Ding et al. (2025), *Modular esterification of unstrained carbonyls through palladium-catalyzed alkyne bridging C-C bond activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64279-0).

title: Independent selection of aromatic rings for saturation
open: Hydrogenate a chosen ring in a molecule containing several electronically similar arenes, with independent control of ring selection and stereochemistry while retaining other reducible groups.
status: Longstanding. Directed ruthenium saturation reported in 2025 selects the arene adjacent to a directing moiety, including complex substrates and gram-scale examples; freely selecting other rings remains open.
why: Provides three-dimensional drug analogues without rebuilding the molecule.
key_works: Yu, Yiu, Zhang and Dong (2025), *Site-selective Ru-catalysed saturation of unactivated arenes via directed 6π activation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01404-8).

title: Position-programmable carbon-to-nitrogen ring editing
open: Replace a selected ring carbon with nitrogen in densely substituted arenes or heteroarenes while preserving the remaining substitution pattern. Independently choose between competing replacement positions using practical reagents.
status: Rapidly developing since the early 2020s. Pyridine-to-pyridazine conversion was demonstrated in 2025 through azide introduction and photochemical rearrangement; general positional editing remains open.
why: Makes medicinal scaffold changes possible late in a synthesis.
key_works: Puriņš, Nakahara and Levin (2025), *Bridging the pyridine-pyridazine synthesis gap by skeletal editing*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adx4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adx4762).

title: Stereoretentive atom swaps in crowded saturated heterocycles
open: Exchange oxygen for nitrogen in highly substituted saturated heterocycles, including crowded positions, while retaining neighboring configurations and avoiding excess substrate or harsh activation.
status: Aliphatic atom swapping remains less developed than aromatic editing. A 2026 tetrahydrofuran-to-pyrrolidine method identifies difficulty with 2-substituted tetrahydrofurans and requires strongly activating conditions.
why: Opens stereochemically matched analogues of saturated medicinal rings.
key_works: Geng et al. (2026), *Skeletal editing of tetrahydrofurans to pyrrolidines through O-to-N single atom swap*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-71886-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71886-y).

title: Carbon isotope exchange at arbitrary skeletal positions
open: Exchange a chosen skeletal carbon for an isotope-labeled carbon in an intact complex molecule without reconstructing its skeleton, losing stereochemical information or extensively scrambling the label.
status: Direct exchange has advanced for selected functional groups. Vanadium-mediated exchange of terminal alkenes was demonstrated in 2025; buried saturated carbons and arbitrary position selection remain open.
why: Simplifies tracer preparation and quantitative studies of molecular fate.
key_works: Krivovicheva et al. (2025), *Vanadium-Mediated Carbon Isotope Exchange of Terminal Alkenes*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c05880](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c05880).

title: Universal protecting-group-free glycosylation
open: Couple unprotected sugars with independent control of linkage position and anomeric configuration across common and rare monosaccharides, including crowded and branched oligosaccharides.
status: Longstanding. A 2024 aminoboronic-acid platform achieved catalyst-controlled 1,2-cis glycosylation and selected site switching, including pentasaccharides with many free hydroxyls. General linkage–anomer control remains open.
why: Makes defined glycans accessible for biological experiments and materials.
key_works: Dang et al. (2024), *Catalytic glycosylation for minimally protected donors and acceptors*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07695-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07695-4).

title: Addressable epimerization of every sugar stereocenter
open: Invert a selected stereocenter of an unprotected sugar or chosen oligosaccharide residue while preserving all other centers and glycosidic linkages.
status: Selective rare-sugar epimerizations were demonstrated in 2020; 2026 kinetic-network control extended selected transformations, including GlcNAc-to-GalNAc. Independent access to every position in complex glycans remains unresolved.
why: Converts abundant sugars into otherwise costly stereochemical building blocks.
key_works: Wang, Carder and Wendlandt (2020), *Synthesis of rare sugar isomers through site-selective epimerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-020-1937-1).

title: Stereodivergent synthesis of distant acyclic stereocenters
open: Access every configuration of several independently positioned, nonadjacent acyclic stereocenters from the same starting-material set without redesigning the route for each isomer.
status: A multidecade objective. Nickel chain-walking chemistry reported online in 2025 accesses all four stereoisomers for selected 1,3- and 1,4-related centers; longer distances and more centers remain open.
why: Separates stereochemical effects from scaffold effects during drug discovery.
key_works: Ju et al. (2025/2026), *Stereodivergent construction of non-adjacent stereocentres via migratory functionalization of alkenes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01994-7).

title: Enantioconvergent alkyl–alkyl coupling across steric classes
open: Couple two unactivated alkyl electrophiles enantioconvergently across primary, secondary and hindered tertiary partners while suppressing homocoupling, elimination and uncontrolled radical escape.
status: Alkyl cross-electrophile coupling has advanced over the past decade. A 2023 demonstration established enantioselective coupling of unactivated halides; broad partner interchangeability remains open.
why: Builds saturated stereochemical complexity from inexpensive fragments.
key_works: Zhao and Shu (2023), *Enantioselective Csp3-Csp3 formation by nickel-catalyzed enantioconvergent cross-electrophile alkyl-alkyl coupling of unactivated alkyl halides*, [primary paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10328415/).

title: Programmable multisite arene defluorofunctionalization
open: Replace a specified subset of fluorines on a polyfluoroarene with different groups in a prescribed order, retaining the other fluorines as successive edits change ring electronics.
status: A longstanding selectivity problem. Boryl-radical chemistry in 2026 expanded transformations from hexa- through difluoroarenes; arbitrary ordered multisite editing remains unresolved.
why: Expands fluorinated scaffolds for medicinal and electronic-material synthesis.
key_works: Ye et al. (2026), *Diverse radical C–F functionalizations of hexa- to difluoroarenes using boryl radicals as link-and-lose mediators*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-026-02137-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02137-2).

title: Position-selective editing of aliphatic C–F bonds
open: Functionalize a selected C–F bond within a multiply fluorinated chain, including unactivated positions, while controlling stereochemistry and the number of fluorines removed.
status: A longstanding organofluorine challenge. Photoredox/cobalt defluoroallylation in 2026 selectively coupled polyfluoroalkyl substrates with alkenes; arbitrary remote-site control remains open.
why: Enables controlled diversification of fluorinated drug and materials scaffolds.
key_works: Ren et al. (2026), *Radical defluoroallylation of polyfluoroalkyl compounds with alkenes via synergistic photoredox/cobalt catalysis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-68840-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68840-3).

title: General mild catalytic amidation without coupling reagents
open: Condense diverse unactivated acids and amines catalytically under mild, concentrated conditions, including hindered and unprotected substrates, with negligible racemization and no stoichiometric activator.
status: Decades old. Phosphorus/catechol catalysis reported in 2025 adds a direct-amidation platform; jointly achieving broad scope, water tolerance, low temperature and catalyst recovery remains open.
why: Removes major reagent and purification burdens from pharmaceutical synthesis.
key_works: Nagano et al. (2025), *Study on Phosphorus Compound/Catechol-Catalyzed Dehydrative Amidation and Its Database Development for Machine Learning*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500955](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500955).

title: Regio- and stereocontrolled hydroamination of hindered internal alkenes
open: Add unprotected alkylamines across hindered, unactivated internal alkenes with independently selectable regio- and enantioselectivity, without nitrogen-partner preactivation.
status: A longstanding hydrofunctionalization target. Amine/ammonium buffering improved anti-Markovnikov hydroamination in 2026; comprehensive internal-alkene scope and stereocontrol remain unresolved.
why: Converts simple olefin feedstocks directly into stereodefined amines.
key_works: Shen et al. (2026), *Amine/ammonium buffering enables efficient anti-Markovnikov hydroamination of olefins with alkylamines*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75644-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75644-y).

title: General modular assembly of stereochemically complex small molecules
open: Extend iterative building-block synthesis to diverse saturated, branched and stereochemically dense molecules with predictable coupling, purification and stereochemical fidelity across long sequences.
status: Modular small-molecule synthesis has developed for over a decade. A 2024 automated platform improved assembly speed; unrestricted topology and stereochemical scope remain open.
why: Broadens automated synthesis beyond structures suited to repeated cross-coupling.
key_works: Wang et al. (2024), *Rapid automated iterative small-molecule synthesis*, [DOI:10.1038/s44160-024-00558-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44160-024-00558-w).

title: Individually addressable carborane vertices
open: Functionalize any chosen non-equivalent boron vertex of a carborane cage, including sequential different substitutions, with controlled cage and substituent stereochemistry.
status: A longstanding cluster-synthesis problem. A 2025 rhodium-carbene method achieved site- and enantioselective B–H insertion for selected carboranes; complete vertex addressability remains unavailable.
why: Expands three-dimensional pharmacophores, ligands and electronically unusual materials.
key_works: Lee et al. (2025), *Site- and enantioselective B−H functionalization of carboranes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-59410-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59410-0).

title: General aluminium redox cross-coupling catalysis
open: Develop broadly useful aluminium-catalyzed cross-couplings completing substrate activation, selective bond formation, product release and catalyst regeneration under functional-group-tolerant conditions.
status: Aluminium redox turnover is established: a 2026 Al(I)/Al(III) alkyne-cyclotrimerization cycle reached turnover numbers up to 2,290. General cross-coupling remains open.
why: Could transfer scarce-metal catalytic functions to an abundant main-group element.
key_works: Zhang and Liu (2026), *Aluminium redox catalysis enables cyclotrimerization of alkynes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09941-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09941-9).

title: Main-group carbonylation with complete catalytic turnover
open: Build main-group carbonylation cycles that repeatedly insert CO, selectively transfer the resulting acyl group and regenerate the catalyst without stoichiometric metal consumption.
status: Reversible main-group CO insertion and extrusion remain sparsely developed. Bismuth compounds enabled reversible visible-light-driven steps in 2025; broadly useful complete synthesis cycles remain open.
why: Provides new catalyst architectures for carbonyl-containing chemicals.
key_works: Geist et al. (2025), *Diaryl Bismuthides and Acyl Bismuthanes Enable Visible-Light-Induced Reversible Carbon Monoxide Insertion and Extrusion*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66412-5).

title: Direct catalytic assembly of configurationally stable germanium stereocenters
open: Construct varied Ge-centered stereogenic molecules directly and catalytically from simple precursors, with predictable configurational stability during subsequent transformations.
status: Main-group stereochemistry remains unevenly developed. A 2025 alkylation/desymmetrization strategy reached chiral germanium centers in four steps; general direct assembly and stereoretentive elaboration remain open.
why: Opens element-centered chirality for ligands, pharmaceuticals and optical materials.
key_works: Wang, Liu and Dong (2025), *Synthesis of chiral germanium center enabled by poly-deborylative alkylation and desymmetrization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-60397-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60397-x).

title: Broad photochemical deracemization without molecular damage
open: Convert racemates to either chosen enantiomer across diverse stereogenic motifs while preserving other stereocenters and photolabile groups, with efficient photon use and practical temperatures.
status: Rapidly expanding since the 2010s. Copper-catalyzed photoderacemization in 2025 covered secondary and tertiary alkyl halides, including tetrasubstituted centers; general transferability remains open.
why: Converts an entire racemate into a selected enantiomer without simple resolution’s yield limitation.
key_works: Zhong et al. (2025), *Photoinduced copper-catalysed deracemization of alkyl halides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08784-8).

title: Durable iron photoredox catalysis with predictable selectivity
open: Design iron photocatalysts that retain activity during prolonged operation and predictably favor coupling over reduction, fragmentation or catalyst degradation across varied substrates.
status: A growing alternative to precious-metal photoredox chemistry. Green-light Fe(III)-NHC catalysis enabled aromatic substitution in 2025; competing hydrodehalogenation illustrates the remaining selectivity problem.
why: Reduces catalyst supply constraints and expands visible-light synthesis.
key_works: de Groot et al. (2025), *Base-Promoted Homolytic Aromatic Substitution (BHAS) Reactions and Hydrodehalogenations Driven by Green Light and an Iron(III)-NHC Photoredox Catalyst*, [DOI:10.1002/chem.202500409](https://doi.org/10.1002/chem.202500409).

title: Solar-intensity photon upconversion with long-term air stability
open: Combine efficient low-intensity upconversion with sustained operation in air, solid-state processability and resistance to photochemical aging under realistic solar spectra.
status: Solid-state operation at sunlight-level excitation was demonstrated in 2026 using sterically protected emitters. Long-duration oxygen tolerance and device-scale stability remain joint targets.
why: Makes lower-energy light usable for photochemistry and optical devices.
key_works: Harada et al. (2026), *Sterically protected π-electron systems for efficient solid-state photon upconversion*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-73898-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73898-0).

title: Transferable photochemical scale-up with preserved selectivity
open: Predict reactor geometry, illumination, mixing and residence-time distributions that preserve selectivity during scale-up, including absorbing, multiphase and precipitating mixtures.
status: Scale-up remains reaction-specific despite industrial successes. A 2025 helicene study compared batch and flow operation; broadly transferable scaling rules remain open.
why: Prevents useful photoreactions from failing during manufacturing development.
key_works: Hewitt et al. (2025), *Scaling Helicene Synthesis via Photochemical Oxidation—A Comparison between Batch and Flow Reactors*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.oprd.5c00038](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.oprd.5c00038).

title: Efficient chemical motors under sustained useful loads
open: Engineer fully synthetic, chemically fueled motors delivering sustained work against external loads with quantified fuel-to-work efficiency, reliability and controllable speed.
status: Synthetic motors have developed for decades. Catalysis-driven polymer-gel contraction was demonstrated in 2025; efficient reusable operation under diverse prescribed loads remains open.
why: Turns molecular motion into useful actuation and transport.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *Transducing chemical energy through catalysis by an artificial molecular motor*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08288-x).

title: Predictable light-to-work conversion in molecular rotary motors
open: Predict and optimize usable work per absorbed photon across complete rotary cycles, including backsteps, solvent effects, thermal relaxation and load coupling.
status: Light-driven motors date to 1999. A 2026 motor used constitutional changes and proton transfer to retain substantial absorbed energy; predictable repeated mechanical output remains open.
why: Connects molecular photophysics to actuator performance.
key_works: Biswas et al. (2026), *A supercharged molecular motor operating by constitutional alteration and proton transfer*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-026-02141-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02141-6).

title: Autonomous molecular pumping between macroscopic reservoirs
open: Integrate artificial pumps into systems that continuously move selected molecules between separate reservoirs against chemical-potential gradients, with useful throughput and low leakage.
status: Autonomous pumping exists in model systems. A 2026 light-driven pump moved macrocycles from solution into an intramolecular compartment; practical reservoir-to-reservoir transport remains open.
why: Enables active separations and light-powered molecular transport.
key_works: Nicoli et al. (2026), *An Artificial Molecular Pump Powered by Light*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.8103353](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.8103353).

title: Reusable programmable molecular assemblers
open: Build molecular machines that repeatedly assemble prescribed products from freely supplied building blocks, release products, reset and maintain sequence and stereochemical fidelity over many cycles.
status: Sequence-directed and stereodivergent synthesis have proof-of-principle demonstrations. A 2017 programmable machine controlled stereochemical outcomes; reusable operation across longer programs remains open.
why: Establishes molecular manufacturing with programmable product identity.
key_works: Kassem et al. (2017), *Stereodivergent synthesis with a programmable molecular machine*, [DOI:10.1038/nature23677](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature23677).

title: Synthesis of chosen molecular knot topologies
open: Translate specified knot or branched-knot topologies into practical designs and high-yield syntheses, including low-symmetry structures lacking convenient templated precursors.
status: Molecular knots have been synthesized for decades. A 2026 bifurcated knot combined three classical crossings and twenty bifurcated junctions; general topology-to-molecule synthesis remains open.
why: Allows systematic tests of topology’s effects on stability, recognition and mechanics.
key_works: Dobson et al. (2026), *Assembly of a bifurcated knot via sequence selective imine condensation*, [DOI:10.1038/s44160-026-01115-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44160-026-01115-3).

title: Long prescribed ring sequences in polyrotaxanes
open: Assemble many chemically distinct rings along an axle in a prescribed order, with low positional error, controlled spacing and reliable synthesis.
status: Mechanical-bond sequence control remains immature. Dual molecular pumps selected translational isomers of [2]- and [3]rotaxanes in 2025; long heterogeneous ring sequences remain open.
why: Enables mechanically encoded information and designed sliding responses.
key_works: Lee et al. (2025), *Controlled assembly of rotaxane translational isomers using dual molecular pumps*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-61364-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61364-2).

title: Switchable aqueous recognition of closely similar polar molecules
open: Design receptors that reversibly distinguish close polar analogues and enantiomers in competitive aqueous mixtures, including unmodified guests, while retaining switchability and useful affinity.
status: A decades-old problem. Photoswitchable glucose-derived receptors discriminated selected amino-acid esters in water in 2025; unesterified guests and complex mixtures remain broader challenges.
why: Supports selective sensing, capture and aqueous separation.
key_works: Most et al. (2025), *Glucose-derived receptors for photo-controlled binding of amino acid esters in water*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-025-01445-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-025-01445-x).

title: High-porosity liquids without prohibitive viscosity
open: Increase accessible permanent cavity density in porous liquids while retaining low viscosity, rapid guest transport and stable porosity through repeated loading cycles.
status: Porous liquids were proposed in 2007. Kilogram-scale type-I liquids were reported in 2025, but increasing cage content strongly increased viscosity in that system.
why: Makes permanently porous fluids practical for separations and flow catalysis.
key_works: Tan et al. (2025), *Direct liquefying organic cages into porous liquid molecules for enhanced near-infrared photothermal conversion and catalysis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63126-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63126-6).

title: Continuously operating dissipative assemblies without waste poisoning
open: Sustain chemically fueled assemblies and their functions through many turnovers while removing or regenerating waste, preventing poisoning and retaining predictable nonequilibrium behavior.
status: Dissipative assembly expanded over the past decade. Fuel-driven transient droplets and macroscopic transport were demonstrated in 2024/2025; continuous operation with integrated waste management remains open.
why: Enables adaptive materials that perform sustained work.
key_works: Liu et al. (2024/2025), *Molecular-scale dissipative chemistry drives the formation of nanoscale assemblies and their macroscale transport*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01665-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01665-z).

title: Long arbitrary sequence-defined synthetic polymers
open: Produce long polymers from a nonstereogenic monomer alphabet with individually prescribed monomer identities and negligible sequence errors at useful scale, avoiding purification after every incorporation.
status: Sequence-defined synthesis has advanced for decades. A 2025 sulfur-exchange method produced defined oligomers up to thirteen units; unrestricted long individual sequences remain open.
why: Enables molecular information storage and designed intrachain interactions.
key_works: Han et al. (2025), *Synthesis of chiral sequence-defined oligomers via sulfur–fluoride and sulfur–phenolate exchange reactions*, [DOI:10.1038/s44160-025-00805-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44160-025-00805-8).

title: Independent sequence and stereochemical programming of polymers
open: Independently specify stereogenic configurations along an already prescribed long-chain connectivity sequence, beyond repeating motifs or stereoregular blocks.
status: Longstanding. A 2025 ring-opening polymerization platform controlled stereochemistry and sequence sufficiently to produce selected AB and ABA materials; arbitrary joint programming remains open.
why: Separates composition, ordering and chirality effects on material properties.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *High-performance recyclable polymers enabled by stereo- and sequence-controlled polymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6).

title: Universal tacticity control in radical polymerization
open: Control tacticity across diverse vinyl monomers, including strongly polar substituents, without requiring special bulky pendant groups followed by their replacement.
status: A longstanding gap. Pan and Ouchi obtained approximately 99% meso-dyad polyacrylamides in 2025 using a transformable bulky pendant; general direct control remains open.
why: Combines practical radical processing with precision thermal and mechanical properties.
key_works: Pan and Ouchi (2025), *Post-polymerization modification enabling library synthesis of highly isotactic polyacrylamides carrying different pendant groups*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-025-01663-3).

title: High-productivity coordination copolymerization of polar vinyl monomers
open: Copolymerize ethylene with diverse unprotected polar vinyl monomers at useful incorporation levels while retaining productivity, high molecular weight and branching/sequence control.
status: Decades old because polar groups interfere with coordination catalysts. Binuclear nickel chemistry converted ethylene/acrylamide feeds into cyano-functionalized polyethylene in 2025; broad compatibility remains open.
why: Introduces adhesion, compatibility and reactivity during polyolefin synthesis.
key_works: Yu et al. (2025), *Cyano-functionalized polyethylenes from ethylene/acrylamide copolymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-57489-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-57489-z).

title: Competitive recyclable non-isocyanate polyurethane foams
open: Combine rapid foaming and curing, low density, controlled cells, durable performance and repeatable recycling in non-isocyanate foams at competitive cost.
status: A multiyear replacement program. Lignin-based foams demonstrated chemical recycling in 2023, including recovered-precursor reuse; the complete performance package across variable feedstocks remains open.
why: Offers practical alternatives to conventional polyurethane production and disposal.
key_works: Sternberg and Pilla (2023), *Chemical recycling of a lignin-based non-isocyanate polyurethane foam*, [DOI:10.1038/s41893-022-01022-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-022-01022-3).

title: Fast vitrimer processing with lifetime creep resistance
open: Make covalent adaptable networks that reshape rapidly during processing yet resist creep throughout service, including humidity, sustained loads, heating cycles and catalyst aging.
status: Central since vitrimer development in the 2010s. NHC-mediated siloxane exchange strongly reduced creep in a 2025 system; transferable lifetime performance remains open.
why: Makes reprocessable thermosets suitable for demanding structural applications.
key_works: Debsharma et al. (2025), *Eliminating creep in vitrimers using temperature-resilient siloxane exchange chemistry and N-heterocyclic carbenes*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC06278G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC06278G).

title: Mechanophore selectivity across realistic loading histories
open: Predict and control force-responsive bond activation under multiaxial, cyclic, impact and heterogeneous loading while preventing unintended backbone damage.
status: Polymer mechanochemistry has developed for decades. Mechanophore cross-links improved ballistic energy dissipation in 2026; transfer across loading histories and repeated impacts remains open.
why: Enables materials that selectively toughen, report damage or release functionality.
key_works: Sang et al. (2026), *Mechanophore cross-linking enhances ballistic energy dissipation of polymers*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10557-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10557-w).

title: Commodity-level performance and low-energy depolymerizability in one polymer
open: Combine commodity-plastic strength, toughness, barrier properties, service stability and cost with selective low-energy recovery of reusable monomers over repeated cycles.
status: A major design program. Stereo- and sequence-controlled polymers reported in 2025 reproduced selected polyolefin-like mechanics and returned to monomer; the full cost–performance–durability combination remains open.
why: Makes circular polymers competitive in demanding high-volume applications.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *High-performance recyclable polymers enabled by stereo- and sequence-controlled polymerization*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01828-6).

title: Polyethylene-to-ethylene with near-complete carbon recovery
open: Return realistic polyethylene waste predominantly to polymer-grade ethylene with nearly complete carbon recovery, low separation burden, sustained catalyst activity and competitive energy use.
status: A decades-old target. A 2025 two-reactor strategy achieved up to 79% combined ethylene/propylene yield; selective ethylene recovery remains a more specific unresolved goal.
why: Closes the polyethylene loop and reduces fresh-feedstock demand.
key_works: Bi et al. (2025), *Closed-loop recycling of polyethylene to ethylene and propylene via a kinetic decoupling–recoupling strategy*, [DOI:10.1038/s44286-025-00290-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44286-025-00290-y).

title: Polypropylene-to-propylene without large coproduct streams
open: Convert real polypropylene waste selectively into propylene at high carbon yield without large unwanted coproduct streams, excessive reagent co-feed or rapid deactivation.
status: Longstanding. Base-metal ethenolysis in 2024 converted polypropylene and mixed polyolefins to light olefins, including propylene/isobutylene mixtures; propylene-focused circularity remains open.
why: Recovers the original high-volume monomer from polypropylene products.
key_works: Conk et al. (2024), *Polyolefin waste to light olefins with ethylene and base-metal heterogeneous catalysts*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq7316](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq7316).

title: Closing both the carbon and chlorine loops of PVC
open: Process additive-rich PVC while recovering carbon as useful feedstocks and chlorine as a reusable stream, minimizing chlorinated by-products, corrosion and reagent waste.
status: A longstanding circularity blocker. Cascade dechlorination/oxidation in 2025 reduced problematic by-products and produced useful liquids, but included CO₂ formation and did not close both material loops.
why: Makes chlorine-containing plastics compatible with comprehensive material recovery.
key_works: Mao et al. (2025), *Catalytic cascade depolymerization for sustainable recycling of waste polyvinyl chloride*, [DOI:10.1038/s41893-025-01654-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-025-01654-1).

title: Low-waste monomer recovery from mixed polyamide textiles
open: Recover polymerization-grade components from variable nylon-containing blends while recovering companion fibers and minimizing activation reagents, solvents and salt waste.
status: Studied for decades. Methyl-tosylate-assisted alcoholysis reported in 2025 handled selected mixtures, including PET/PA6 textiles; broad feed tolerance and low-waste continuous operation remain open.
why: Makes durable blended textiles compatible with material circularity.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), *Sustainable recycling of polyamides via C–N bond cleavage facilitated by methyl tosylate under mild conditions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64197-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64197-1).

title: Universal closed-loop recycling of heterogeneous polyurethane foams
open: Recycle varied aged polyurethane foams into equivalent-quality foams through many cycles, recovering reagents and preventing incompatible-residue accumulation.
status: Longstanding. A 2025 acetoxime method demonstrated foam-to-foam recycling with recoverable reagent and preserved or improved properties; robustness across commercial formulations remains open.
why: Extends circularity to cross-linked foams that cannot be remelted.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), *Atom economic closed-loop recycling of thermoset polyurethane foams*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-60111-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60111-x).

title: Complete recovery of legacy epoxy composite components
open: Recover high-quality fibers and reusable resin components from existing heterogeneous epoxy composites at scale, with low reagent consumption and solvent-recovery cost.
status: A decades-old problem. Acetolysis in 2025 recovered components from epoxy–amine carbon-fiber composites; diverse cured formulations and manufacturing-scale reuse remain open.
why: Recovers both valuable reinforcement and embedded chemical feedstocks.
key_works: Lahive et al. (2025), *Acetolysis for epoxy-amine carbon fibre-reinforced polymer recycling*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09067-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09067-y).

title: Repeated closed-loop polystyrene recycling from contaminated feed
open: Repeatedly recover polymerization-grade styrene from post-consumer polystyrene while maintaining carbon yield, purity and catalyst performance across varying contaminants.
status: Depolymerization is established. A 2026 microwave-assisted Zn/ZnO study reported approximately 80% styrene yield through five catalyst cycles and repolymerization; variable contaminated-feed operation remains open.
why: Prevents impurities and quality losses from undermining circular polystyrene.
key_works: Zhang et al. (2026), *Efficient depolymerization of polystyrene waste into styrene monomers over the microwave-assisted Zn/b-ZnO catalyst system*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jece.2026.121282](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jece.2026.121282).

title: Continuous low-temperature recycling of commercial polymethacrylates
open: Translate lower-temperature bulk depolymerization into continuous waste treatment with high monomer purity and recovery, reagent regeneration and tolerance of pigments, copolymers and aging products.
status: A 2026 N-hydroxyphthalimide-triggered approach reported rapid, near-quantitative recovery from commercial polymethacrylates. Continuous contaminated-feed operation remains unresolved.
why: Reduces the energy and cost of circular acrylic plastics.
key_works: Whitfield et al. (2026), *Lower-temperature bulk depolymerization of commercial polymethacrylates*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-026-02232-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02232-4).

title: Selective dissolution of variable multilayer plastic waste
open: Recover every valuable layer of variable packaging using reusable solvent systems tolerant of inks, adhesives, fillers and aging without excessive energy demand.
status: Selective dissolution has a long history. The 2020 STRAP process established recovery of multilayer constituents; adapting sequences to unknown post-consumer compositions remains open.
why: Provides recovery routes for high-performance multilayer packaging.
key_works: Walker et al. (2020), *Recycling of multilayer plastic packaging materials by solvent-targeted recovery and precipitation*, [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.aba7599](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aba7599).

title: Repeated mixed-plastic recycling without compatibilizer depletion or impurity buildup
open: Prevent compatibilizer depletion, contaminant accumulation and progressive degradation while preserving processing and mechanical properties through repeated recycling of variable aged mixtures.
status: A longstanding alternative to perfect sorting. A 2025/2026 dynamic-crosslinker platform improved mixed-plastic properties; tolerance to changing composition and accumulated degradation remains open.
why: Turns mixed waste into useful materials when separation is impractical.
key_works: Gao et al. (2025/2026), *Topological universal dynamic compatibilization enhances recycling of mixed plastics*, [DOI:10.1038/s41893-025-01688-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41893-025-01688-5).

title: Selective rubber devulcanization without backbone damage
open: Cleave sulfur cross-links in heterogeneous aged rubber while preserving long chains, then repeatedly revulcanize it into materials meeting demanding virgin-rubber requirements.
status: A decades-old selectivity problem. Choline-based deep eutectic solvents improved selective devulcanization in 2025; broad formulation tolerance with minimal cumulative damage remains open.
why: Retains the material value of cross-linked elastomers.
key_works: Liu et al. (2025), *Selective devulcanization of ground tire rubber by choline-based deep eutectic solvents for high-performance recycled materials*, [primary paper](https://ww-w.expresspolymlett.com/article.php?a=EPL-0013318).

title: Closed-reagent-loop silicone recycling
open: Recycle diverse filled and cross-linked silicones while recovering silicone feedstocks and auxiliary reagents, controlling catalyst loss and impurity accumulation.
status: Gallium/BCl₃ chemistry in 2025 converted varied silicone wastes into key chlorosilanes near quantitatively at 40 °C. Closing auxiliary loops and demonstrating prolonged plant operation remain open.
why: Conserves embedded silicon-processing energy and valuable feedstocks.
key_works: Vu et al. (2025), *Gallium-catalyzed recycling of silicone waste with boron trichloride to yield key chlorosilanes*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adv0919](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adv0919).

title: Elastane recovery from existing blended fabrics
open: Recover useful elastane from already-manufactured, compositionally varied textiles without destroying companion fibers, using scalable low-waste separation.
status: A persistent textile-circularity obstacle. A 2025 chitosan finishing strategy improves future fiber separability; existing unmodified core-spun fabrics remain a distinct challenge.
why: Removes a small component that can obstruct recovery of entire garments.
key_works: Grosvenor et al. (2025), *A roll-to-roll chitosan finishing strategy for elastane recovery*, [DOI:10.1039/D5LP00213C](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5LP00213C).

title: Durable structural adhesives with selective reversible debonding
open: Maintain structural adhesion throughout service, followed by rapid debonding and rebonding under mild triggers that preserve substrates and avoid accidental activation.
status: A longstanding design tension. Reversible biobased adhesives combined strong bonding and rapid thermal detachment in 2025; broad substrate compatibility and repeated structural qualification remain open.
why: Enables repair and disassembly of bonded products.
key_works: Lv et al. (2025), *Reversible biobased adhesives enable closed-loop engineered composites*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-62917-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62917-1).

title: Complete nitrogenase catalytic cycle
open: Determine the structures, protonation states, electron transfers and branching kinetics of every catalytically relevant nitrogenase intermediate under turnover.
status: Decades of spectroscopy constrain the cycle. Calculations in 2026 still test competing electron-transfer mechanisms rather than establish a complete experimentally resolved trajectory.
why: Enables mechanistically informed nitrogen-fixation catalysts.
key_works: Siegbahn (2026), *The mechanism for electron transfer in nitrogenase*, [DOI:10.1039/D6CP02289H](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6CP02289H).

title: Nitrogen fixation during sustained oxygen exposure
open: Engineer nitrogenase maintaining useful turnover during oxygen exposure without costly oxygen removal or permanent protective shutdown.
status: Oxygen sensitivity is longstanding. Structures reported in 2025 explain conformational protection, which does not establish sustained oxygen-tolerant catalysis.
why: Could simplify biological fertilizer production and engineered nitrogen-fixing hosts.
key_works: Narehood et al. (2025), *Structural basis for the conformational protection of nitrogenase from O2*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08311-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08311-1).

title: Reactive oxidant in particulate methane monooxygenase
open: Identify the oxygen-derived species that cleaves methane’s C–H bond in active membrane-bound pMMO and establish its formation and decay kinetics.
status: Structural studies narrowed copper-site assignments. Calculations in 2024–2025 proposed distinguishable oxidant-generation mechanisms requiring decisive turnover experiments.
why: Supplies mechanistic guidance for selective methane oxidation.
key_works: Lundgren et al. (2025), *The CuB site in particulate methane monooxygenase may be used to produce hydrogen peroxide*, [DOI:10.1039/D4DT03301A](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4DT03301A).

title: RuBisCO’s achievable catalytic frontier
open: Establish attainable joint limits of carboxylation speed, CO₂/O₂ specificity, affinity, assembly and stability, then demonstrate improved combinations in relevant cells.
status: Decades of tradeoff arguments remain unsettled. A 2025 sequence–function map broadened accessible variants; improved individual mutants do not establish the global frontier.
why: Could increase photosynthetic carbon fixation without compensating resource costs.
key_works: Prywes et al. (2025), *A map of the rubisco biochemical landscape*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08455-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08455-0).

title: General high-efficiency enzyme design from a reaction specification
open: Design efficient, selective enzymes for mechanistically diverse specified reactions with predictable success and little experimental optimization.
status: Major successes leave the broad target open: a 2025 designed Kemp eliminase reached approximately 30 s⁻¹, and 2026 catalytic-motif scaffolding extended demonstrations to other transformations.
why: Makes biocatalysis available beyond natural enzyme families.
key_works: Listov et al. (2025), *Complete computational design of high-efficiency Kemp elimination enzymes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09136-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09136-2); Braun et al. (2026), *Computational enzyme design by catalytic motif scaffolding*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09747-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09747-9).

title: Predicting distal mutations across a complete catalytic cycle
open: Predict how mutations far from active sites jointly change substrate entry, chemical conversion, product release and overall turnover in previously unseen enzymes.
status: A longstanding design gap. Experiments in 2025 separated active-site and distal effects in three designed Kemp eliminases; a transferable predictor remains open.
why: Captures improvements missed by active-site-only optimization.
key_works: Zarifi et al. (2025), *Distal mutations enhance catalysis in designed enzymes by facilitating substrate binding and product release*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63802-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63802-7).

title: Programmable allostery with specified response curves
open: Design proteins with prescribed ligand-dependent activation, cooperativity, reversibility and cross-talk, retaining these responses inside cells.
status: Allostery has been studied for decades. A 2025 study designed 14 signaling-active receptors; arbitrary response programming remains unestablished.
why: Enables controllable enzymes, biosensors and cellular circuits.
key_works: Chen et al. (2025), *Computational design of highly signalling-active membrane receptors through solvent-mediated allosteric networks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01719-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01719-2).

title: Predictive catalysis in aging biomolecular condensates
open: Predict rates and selectivity from condensate composition, partitioning, age and exchange kinetics, including transitions from catalytic enhancement to inhibition.
status: The field expanded during the 2010s. Synthetic-condensate experiments in 2025 demonstrated time-dependent loss of enhancement; general predictive laws remain open.
why: Connects phase behavior to cellular reaction control.
key_works: Kang et al. (2025), *Time-dependent catalytic activity in aging condensates*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-62074-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62074-5).

title: Sustained autonomous RNA self-replication and evolution
open: Demonstrate a ribozyme system that copies its complete catalytic information and sustains heritable evolution through repeated replication cycles using supplied small substrates.
status: QT45 separately synthesized its own sequence and complementary strand in 2026, at approximately 0.2% yield after 72 days. Sustained autonomous propagation outrunning chemical and mutational losses remains open.
why: Tests a central constructive claim of RNA-world models.
key_works: Papastavrou, Horning and Joyce (2024), *RNA-catalyzed evolution of catalytic RNA*, [DOI:10.1073/pnas.2321592121](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2321592121); Attwater et al. (2025), *Trinucleotide substrates under pH–freeze–thaw cycles enable open-ended exponential RNA replication by a polymerase ribozyme*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01830-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01830-y); Gianni et al. (2026), *A small polymerase ribozyme that can synthesize itself and its complementary strand*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adt2760](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adt2760).

title: Indefinite nonenzymatic RNA replication
open: Couple copying, strand separation and substrate replenishment into repeated enzyme-free replication of mixed-sequence RNA without externally resetting each generation.
status: Chemical copying has advanced for decades. Virtual-circular-genome experiments in 2023 tested a route around duplex trapping without establishing indefinite autonomous replication.
why: Bridges prebiotic synthesis and Darwinian heredity.
key_works: Ding et al. (2023), *Experimental Tests of the Virtual Circular Genome Model for Nonenzymatic RNA Replication*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.3c00612](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.3c00612).

title: Coordinated protocell genome and membrane reproduction
open: Build chemically simple compartments whose genome copying, membrane growth, division and inheritance remain coordinated across many generations without protein machinery.
status: Components have decades of demonstrations. Mixed-sequence RNA copying inside fatty-acid vesicles was shown in 2018; integrated hereditary reproduction remains open.
why: Defines a constructive intermediate between chemistry and cells.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Protocell nutrient entry without genome leakage
open: Obtain membranes admitting replication feedstocks while retaining genetic polymers and remaining stable under the ions and environmental cycles required by copying.
status: The permeability–retention conflict is longstanding. Vesicle experiments in 2018 admitted short oligonucleotides; compatibility across repeated reproduction cycles remains unresolved.
why: Prevents replicating compartments from starving or losing hereditary information.
key_works: O’Flaherty et al. (2018), *Copying of Mixed-Sequence RNA Templates inside Model Protocells*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b00639](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b00639).

title: Self-replenishing prebiotic nucleotide activation
open: Sustain nucleotide activation and reactivation in a copying-compatible network using plausible environmental energy, with explicit accounting for inhibitory by-products.
status: Activation chemistry is decades old. Photochemical activation and recycling were demonstrated in 2018; integration into sustained genome replication remains open.
why: Supplies the chemical free energy consumed by copying.
key_works: Mariani et al. (2018), *A Light-Releasable Potentially Prebiotic Nucleotide Activating Agent*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.8b05189](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.8b05189).

title: Parasite-resistant prebiotic replicator communities
open: Demonstrate chemically simple replicator populations that resist faster parasitic sequences while preserving innovation and cooperation under plausible compartment cycles.
status: Transient compartmentalization suppressed parasite takeover experimentally in 2016. Comparable robustness with wholly prebiotic replication chemistry remains open.
why: Addresses an evolutionary failure mode beyond successful copying.
key_works: Matsumura et al. (2016), *Transient compartmentalization of RNA replicators prevents extinction due to parasites*, [PubMed record](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27940874/).

title: One connected geochemical route to cellular building blocks
open: Demonstrate a connected environmental sequence producing compatible nucleotide, peptide and membrane precursors from realistically impure feeds, with explicit purification and transport accounting.
status: Common precursor chemistry was demonstrated in 2015. Compatibility and selectivity across complete environmental networks remain unresolved.
why: Tests whether individually plausible pathways coexist in one origin scenario.
key_works: Patel et al. (2015), *Common origins of RNA, protein and lipid precursors in a cyanosulfidic protometabolism*, [DOI:10.1038/nchem.2202](https://doi.org/10.1038/nchem.2202).

title: Self-sustaining nonenzymatic protometabolism
open: Construct an environmentally powered network that regenerates intermediates, maintains flux and continuously produces useful precursors.
status: A 2019 iron-promoted network generated nine of eleven Krebs-cycle intermediates; sustained network closure and coupling to heredity remain open.
why: Explains how chemical systems could maintain themselves before enzymes.
key_works: Muchowska, Varma and Moran (2019), *Synthesis and breakdown of universal metabolic precursors promoted by iron*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-019-1151-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-019-1151-1).

title: Emergence of sequence-coded peptide synthesis
open: Show how plausible RNA–peptide systems acquire reproducible sequence-dependent amino-acid assignment and heritable selection for the resulting peptides.
status: A longstanding genetic-code origins problem. Experiments in 2022 demonstrated peptide growth on modified RNA without establishing autonomous coding.
why: Connects RNA-world chemistry to translation.
key_works: Müller et al. (2022), *A prebiotically plausible scenario of an RNA–peptide world*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-022-04676-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-04676-3).

title: Network-wide emergence of biological homochirality
open: Demonstrate a sustained prebiotic network amplifying small chiral imbalances across interacting molecular families while resisting racemization and dilution.
status: Longstanding. A 2025 kinetic model coupled amino-acid synthesis and peptide ligation; experimentally closing such an amplifying network remains open.
why: Explains common handedness supporting recognition and heredity.
key_works: Higgs and Blackmond (2025), *Autocatalytic symmetry breaking and chiral amplification in a feedback network combining amino acid synthesis and ligation*, [DOI:10.1073/pnas.2423683122](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2423683122).

title: Why D-RNA became coupled to L-proteins
open: Identify and discriminate mechanisms establishing the observed relationship between sugar and amino-acid handedness, including historical contingency and chemical bias.
status: A longstanding specificity question. Tests of 15 self-aminoacylating ribozymes in 2024 found both chiral preferences, challenging a universal D-RNA-to-L-amino-acid bias.
why: Explains the particular handedness pairing beyond homochirality itself.
key_works: Kenchel et al. (2024), *Prebiotic chiral transfer from self-aminoacylating ribozymes may favor either handedness*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-52362-x).

title: General single-molecule protein sequencing
open: Read arbitrary intact protein sequences with calibrated errors across all amino acids and relevant modifications, without dependence on narrowly trained sequence families.
status: Multipass nanopore reading of long strands was demonstrated in 2024; stepwise peptide reading added capabilities in 2026. Universal proteome sequencing remains open.
why: Makes sequence and modification information accessible from tiny samples.
key_works: Motone et al. (2024), *Multi-pass, single-molecule nanopore reading of long protein strands*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07935-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07935-7); Chen et al. (2026), *Sequential reading of a stepwise-shortened peptide immobilized on nanopore*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10881-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10881-1).

title: Complete quantitative proteoform inventories
open: Identify and quantify intact protein forms, including combinations of modifications and sequence variants, across defined biological samples with measured coverage.
status: Top-down proteomics has advanced for decades. Comparisons in 2024 still found substantial sample-preparation dependence and incomplete coverage.
why: Resolves molecular states hidden by gene- or peptide-level measurements.
key_works: Kaulich et al. (2024), *Influence of different sample preparation approaches on proteoform identification by top-down proteomics*, [DOI:10.1038/s41592-024-02481-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02481-6).

title: Unbiased single-cell protein copy-number measurement
open: Quantify low- and high-abundance proteins in individual cells with known recovery, missingness and false-discovery rates across cell types.
status: Methods expanded rapidly during the 2010s. The 2025 Chip-Tip workflow increased coverage without achieving a complete unbiased census.
why: Separates biological heterogeneity from detection artifacts.
key_works: Ye et al. (2025), *Enhanced sensitivity and scalability with a Chip-Tip workflow enables deep single-cell proteomics*, [DOI:10.1038/s41592-024-02558-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-024-02558-2).

title: Structural identification of the dark metabolome
open: Assign defensible molecular structures to reproducible unannotated metabolomic signals, distinguishing metabolites from adducts, fragments, contaminants and isomers.
status: A decades-old coverage gap. DeepMet predicted and helped discover mammalian metabolites in 2026; comprehensive experimentally established identification remains open.
why: Reveals unrecognized pathways, biomarkers and exposures.
key_works: Qiang et al. (2026), *Language model-guided anticipation and discovery of mammalian metabolites*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09969-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09969-x).

title: Assigning enzymes to unknown metabolic transformations
open: Convert isotope-linked metabolite transformations into validated reaction mechanisms and enzyme assignments, including compartment and physiological context.
status: Isotope tracing has long constrained pathways. A 2025 workflow mapped unknown reactions, leaving many causal assignments unresolved.
why: Converts chemical associations into functional biochemistry.
key_works: Gao et al. (2025), *Charting unknown metabolic reactions by mass spectrometry-resolved stable-isotope tracing metabolomics*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-60258-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-60258-7).

title: General sequencing of branched native glycans
open: Determine monosaccharide identity, linkage position, anomeric configuration and branching for arbitrary glycans in mixtures, with calibrated structural ambiguity.
status: A longstanding structural problem. Enzymatic nanopore decoding in 2025 and fragment reassembly in 2026 established partial routes; universal sequencing remains open.
why: Enables complete characterization of glycoproteins and cell-surface recognition chemistry.
key_works: Xia et al. (2026), *Nanopore-Based Glycan Sequencing via a Fragmentation-Reassembly Strategy*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c22760](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c22760).

title: Simultaneous nanoplastic identity, size and abundance
open: Quantify individual environmental nanoplastics by polymer chemistry, size and particle number while rejecting mineral and biological interferents.
status: The gap became prominent during the 2010s. Optical sieves advanced sizing and counting in 2025; broad chemical identification in complex matrices remains unresolved.
why: Makes exposure measurements comparable and interpretable.
key_works: Ludescher et al. (2025), *Optical sieve for nanoplastic detection, sizing and counting*, [DOI:10.1038/s41566-025-01733-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-025-01733-x).

title: Representative certified nanoplastic reference materials
open: Produce traceable references spanning weathered polymers, irregular shapes, additive mixtures, sizes and environmental matrices, with independently certified properties.
status: Reference materials already exist. Work published online in 2025 introduced laser-generated model particles and discussed NPPP-1; representative coverage and cross-method certification remain incomplete.
why: Enables reproducible recovery estimates, method comparison and dose–response experiments.
key_works: Pegoraro et al. (2026; online 2025), *Nanoplastic reference materials for biological and methodological assessment*, [DOI:10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2](https://doi.org/10.1186/s43591-025-00157-2).

title: Closing organofluorine mass balances in complex products
open: Reconcile total, extractable, inorganic, polymeric and individually identified fluorine in realistic products and environmental samples within validated uncertainties.
status: Targeted PFAS assays leave unidentified fractions. A 2018 cosmetics study demonstrated substantial mass-balance gaps; general analytical closure remains open.
why: Prevents targeted testing from overlooking major fluorinated reservoirs.
key_works: Schultes et al. (2018), *Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances and fluorine mass balance in cosmetic products from the Swedish market: implications for environmental emissions and human exposure*, [DOI:10.1039/C8EM00368H](https://doi.org/10.1039/C8EM00368H).

title: Low-energy destruction of mixed PFAS waste
open: Mineralize diverse PFAS mixtures in real wastes with closed fluorine balances, low energy and reagent demand, and no persistent fluorinated escape products.
status: PFCA mineralization was demonstrated in 2022 and phosphate-assisted mechanochemistry in 2025; treatment across all relevant structures and matrices remains open.
why: Turns capture into permanent contaminant removal.
key_works: Trang et al. (2022), *Low-temperature mineralization of perfluorocarboxylic acids*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abm8868](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abm8868); Yang et al. (2025), *Phosphate-enabled mechanochemical PFAS destruction for fluoride reuse*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08698-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08698-5).

title: Circular recovery of fluorine from contaminated waste
open: Recover fluorine from variable contaminated PFAS wastes as reusable feedstock while meeting purity and net-resource requirements over repeated cycles.
status: Fluoride reuse was demonstrated in 2025. Feed variability, separation burdens and full process economics remain unresolved.
why: Couples remediation to reduced demand for primary fluorine resources.
key_works: Yang et al. (2025), *Phosphate-enabled mechanochemical PFAS destruction for fluoride reuse*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-08698-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-08698-5).

title: Tire antiozonants without hazardous transformation products
open: Replace 6PPD with chemistry preserving tire durability and road safety while avoiding comparably hazardous parent compounds, transformation products and emissions.
status: 6PPD-quinone toxicity was identified in 2020–2021. California’s alternatives-analysis process documents continuing evaluation rather than an established universal substitute.
why: Reduces aquatic harm while maintaining tire performance.
key_works: Tian et al. (2021), *A ubiquitous tire rubber-derived chemical induces acute mortality in coho salmon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abd6951](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abd6951); California DTSC, [*Motor Vehicle Tires Containing 6PPD*](https://dtsc.ca.gov/scp/motor_vehicle_tires_containing_6ppd/).

title: Predictive environmental transformation network for PPD antiozonants
open: Predict parent loss, product formation, persistence and transport across sunlight, redox, mineral and dissolved-organic-matter conditions, with validated mass balances.
status: Individual pathways have accumulated since the 6PPD-quinone discovery. Measurements in 2025 resolved thermal and photochemical reactions; a transferable field network remains open.
why: Identifies hazards missed by parent-compound monitoring.
key_works: Platt et al. (2025), *Aquatic Thermal and Photochemical Reactivity of N-(1,3-Dimethylbutyl)-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (6PPD), N-Isopropyl-N′-phenyl-p-phenylenediamine (IPPD), and 6PPD-quinone*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c12896](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c12896).

title: Atmospheric hydroxyl-radical budget after interference correction
open: Close OH production and loss budgets across environments using independent, interference-tested instruments and chemically complete mechanisms.
status: Discrepancies have persisted for decades. A 2025 reassessment showed instrumental interferences can explain some excesses; the evidence does not establish a universal missing source.
why: Constrains atmospheric methane lifetime and pollutant formation.
key_works: Price et al. (2025), *Re-assessing hydroxyl radical chemistry in the atmosphere: Instrument interferences may explain previous measurement discrepancies*, [DOI:10.1038/s43247-025-02308-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-025-02308-y).

title: Isoprene-derived particles from molecular clusters to clouds
open: Predict nucleation, growth, survival and cloud-nucleating activity of isoprene oxidation products across realistic temperatures, humidity, NOₓ and aerosol mixtures.
status: Upper-tropospheric studies in 2024 provided major mechanistic support. Globally validated predictions of particle survival and cloud effects remain open.
why: Reduces uncertainty in chemically mediated cloud effects.
key_works: Shen et al. (2024), *New particle formation from isoprene under upper-tropospheric conditions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-08196-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-08196-0).

title: Molecular causes of marine dissolved-organic-carbon persistence
open: Determine which structures, concentrations and ecological contexts cause dissolved organic carbon to persist, and predict turnover under changing ocean conditions.
status: A decades-old puzzle. Phytoplankton experiments in 2025 linked producers to distinct carbon pools without resolving molecule-specific global lifetimes.
why: Connects molecular chemistry to a major carbon reservoir.
key_works: Lu et al. (2025), *The role of phytoplankton in structuring global oceanic dissolved organic carbon pools*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63105-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63105-x).

title: Adjacent-lanthanide separation with low resource consumption
subfield: Separation chemistry and chemical process science
open: Separate difficult neighboring lanthanides from realistic multicomponent feeds using few stages, recyclable reagents, high recovery and demonstrably lower resource demand.
status: A longstanding chemical-similarity problem. Lanmodulin studies in 2023 and 2026 improved selectivity, including Pr/La discrimination; they do not solve every adjacent-element separation.
why: Reduces waste and supply constraints for critical materials.
key_works: Mattocks et al. (2023), *Enhanced rare-earth separation with a metal-sensitive lanmodulin dimer*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-05945-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-05945-5); Diep et al. (2026), *A family portrait of lanmodulin selectivity for enhanced rare-earth separations*, [DOI:10.1038/s41589-026-02176-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41589-026-02176-3).

title: Lithium–magnesium separation across actual brine compositions
subfield: Separation chemistry and chemical process science
open: Maintain lithium recovery, purity, throughput and membrane life across real brines containing variable magnesium, sodium, boron, organics and scaling species.
status: Membranes work in selected feeds. Studies in 2025 clarified favorable partitioning in negatively charged membranes; broad process robustness remains open.
why: Makes direct lithium extraction less dependent on favorable source chemistry.
key_works: Santiago-Pagán et al. (2025), *Selective partitioning and uphill transport enable effective Li/Mg ion separation by negatively charged membranes*, [DOI:10.1038/s44286-025-00312-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44286-025-00312-9).

title: Durable nanofiltration across solvent families
subfield: Separation chemistry and chemical process science
open: Produce scalable membranes retaining selectivity and useful flux through mixed polar/nonpolar solvents, reactive impurities, cleaning and prolonged operation.
status: Decades of development led to faster broad-solvent demonstrations in 2025; transferable lifetime and fouling performance remain incomplete.
why: Replaces energy-intensive evaporation in suitable processes.
key_works: Wu et al. (2025), *Microstructure engineering of polyamide membranes for ultrafast polar and non-polar solvent transport*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63663-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63663-0).

title: Predictive multicomponent transport through swelling membranes
subfield: Separation chemistry and chemical process science
open: Predict coupled solvent and solute fluxes from membrane chemistry across composition-dependent swelling and plasticization without refitting each mixture.
status: Competing transport descriptions are longstanding. Theory, simulations and experiments in 2024 established important solvent-flow mechanisms; universal mixture prediction remains open.
why: Makes membrane selection and process design less empirical.
key_works: Fan et al. (2024), *The physical basis for solvent flow in organic solvent nanofiltration*, [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.ado4332](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.ado4332).

title: Molecular structures and reaction networks of melanoidins
open: Determine connectivity and formation pathways of heterogeneous food melanoidins sufficiently to predict color, aroma release and reactivity from processing conditions.
status: Maillard chemistry has been studied for over a century. Fractionation and spectroscopy in 2025 resolved structural features without establishing complete heterogeneous structures.
why: Enables controlled browning and interpretation of processing products.
key_works: Wang et al. (2025), *Molecular structure characteristics and pyrolytic volatiles of hydrosoluble colored fractions from three melanoidins*, [DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-02108-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-02108-6).

title: Predicting odors of concentration-dependent mixtures
open: Predict perceived odor quality and intensity from mixtures, concentrations and individual variation, including masking, synergy and emergent percepts.
status: Structure–odor prediction is longstanding. A 2023 principal odor map generalized across molecular tasks; realistic mixture perception remains a broader target.
why: Connects chemical formulation to reproducible flavor and fragrance design.
key_works: Lee et al. (2023), *A principal odor map unifies diverse tasks in olfactory perception*, [DOI:10.1126/science.ade4401](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ade4401).

title: Predicting oil-paint and acrylic-ground interfacial failure
open: Predict when pigment–binder–ground combinations develop cracks, protrusions or delamination from measured chemistry and environmental history.
status: Many degradation reactions are known. Interface-resolved analyses in 2025 linked early damage to chemical changes; a generally predictive lifetime model remains open.
why: Supports preventive conservation before irreversible visible damage.
key_works: Gnemmi et al. (2025), *Early degradation mechanisms at the interface between acrylic grounds and oil paint films*, [DOI:10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-025-01861-1).

title: Accelerated-aging tests that predict reversible conservation performance
open: Relate accelerated light and heat exposure to decades of natural aging while predicting color stability and future safe removal of retouching materials.
status: Extrapolation is longstanding. A 2025 comparison of six paints used accelerated exposure and four years of natural aging, finding formulation-dependent behavior.
why: Prevents restorations that later discolor or become difficult to remove.
key_works: Bucki, Zwinczak and Kruczała (2025), *Research into physicochemical changes in the retouching paints used at the National Museum in Krakow*, [DOI:10.1038/s40494-025-01720-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s40494-025-01720-z).

title: Representative records of unsuccessful chemical experiments
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Build reusable datasets of failed and low-yield reactions with complete conditions, analytical limits, execution deviations and representative sampling of attempted chemistry.
status: A 2016 study demonstrated the value of failed materials experiments. Collection remains dependent on local notebooks and selective disclosure.
why: Reduces success-only bias in prediction and discovery.
key_works: Raccuglia et al. (2016), *Machine-learning-assisted materials discovery using failed experiments*, [DOI:10.1038/nature17439](https://doi.org/10.1038/nature17439).

title: Leakage-resistant prospective reaction benchmarks
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Establish prospective benchmarks separated by reaction family, laboratory, time and procedure, including failures and costs, with independent experimental reproduction.
status: Reaction benchmarks exist. ORDerly improved open-data cleaning and evaluation in 2024; broad prospective assessment remains incomplete.
why: Measures useful generalization to new chemistry.
key_works: Wigh et al. (2024), *ORDerly: Data Sets and Benchmarks for Chemical Reaction Data*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00292](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.4c00292).

title: Portable execution of chemical procedures across laboratories
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Execute the same chemically specified procedure on different hardware and in independent laboratories with comparable product identity, yield and purity, recording deviations.
status: Modular robotic synthesis was demonstrated in 2019. General transfer still requires resolving equipment semantics, mixing, sensing and tacit procedural details.
why: Makes reproducibility and shared automated experimentation practical.
key_works: Steiner et al. (2019), *Organic synthesis in a modular robotic system driven by a chemical programming language*, [DOI:10.1126/science.aav2211](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aav2211).

title: Interoperable reaction records linked to raw evidence
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Connect reaction identities, material lots, conditions, time series, spectra, workup and product assignments in interoperable records preserving uncertainty and provenance.
status: The 2021 Open Reaction Database supplies a substantial schema and repository; complete cross-instrument capture and broad adoption remain unfinished.
why: Permits reanalysis, auditing and learning from actual experiments.
key_works: Kearnes et al. (2021), *The Open Reaction Database*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.1c09820](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.1c09820).

title: Sustainable stewardship of open chemical reference data
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Establish durable funding, governance and maintenance that keep chemical datasets, standards, identifiers and executable tools usable beyond individual grants and across countries.
status: Funded initiatives exist: NFDI4Chem began in 2020 and published a 2025–2030 proposal. Durable international coverage remains incomplete.
why: Prevents loss of reusable scientific evidence and standards.
key_works: Steinbeck et al. (2020), *NFDI4Chem—Towards a National Research Data Infrastructure for Chemistry in Germany*, [DOI:10.3897/rio.6.e55852](https://doi.org/10.3897/rio.6.e55852); NFDI4Chem, [2025–2030 proposal](https://zenodo.org/records/17747150).

title: Globally reconcilable commercial-chemical inventories
subfield: Chemical data, automation and research infrastructure
open: Reconcile substance identities, mixtures, uses, production information and hazard evidence across national inventories, with useful transparency under confidentiality constraints.
status: A 2020 comparison of 22 inventories documented major identity and information gaps. Comprehensive interoperable coverage remains an infrastructure target.
why: Makes chemical-exposure accounting and substitution priorities tractable.
key_works: Wang, Walker, Muir and Nagatani-Yoshida (2020), *Toward a Global Understanding of Chemical Pollution: A First Comprehensive Analysis of National and Regional Chemical Inventories*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.9b06379](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.9b06379).

title: Optimal Lieb–Oxford constant
open: Determine the smallest universal constant bounding the indirect Coulomb energy by the integral of the electron density to the four-thirds power. Distinguish the unrestricted bound from exchange-only bounds and bounds for restricted physical states.
status: Open since the 1981 inequality. Lewin, Lieb and Seiringer’s 2022 proof gives an upper bound of approximately 1.58; the reported lower bound exceeds 1.44.
why: A sharper exact constraint would improve the mathematical foundation of exchange–correlation approximations.
key_works: M. Lewin, E. H. Lieb and R. Seiringer (2022), *Improved Lieb–Oxford bound on the indirect and exchange energies*, [arXiv:2203.12473](https://arxiv.org/abs/2203.12473), DOI: 10.1007/s11005-022-01584-5.

title: Transferable orbital-free kinetic-energy functional
open: Construct an orbital-free kinetic-energy functional whose optimized densities, forces and dissociation curves remain accurate across unfamiliar molecules, charge states and bonding environments. Demonstrate a scaling advantage after counting training and density optimization.
status: The kinetic-energy closure has obstructed molecular orbital-free calculations for decades. Deep learning produced substantial molecular progress in 2024; broad chemical transferability remains unresolved.
why: It could extend accurate electronic-structure simulation to much larger reactive systems.
key_works: H. Zhang et al. (2024), *Overcoming the barrier of orbital-free density functional theory for molecular systems using deep learning*, [DOI:10.1038/s43588-024-00605-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43588-024-00605-8); [arXiv:2309.16578](https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16578).

title: Practical density functional satisfying the full flat-plane condition
open: Build an affordable functional that simultaneously respects piecewise linearity in electron number and constancy for fractional spin while giving reliable energies, densities and forces across bond breaking. Avoid case-specific corrections and artificial symmetry breaking.
status: Fractional-charge and fractional-spin failures were unified in 2008–2009. Fractional-spin corrections demonstrated successful molecular examples in 2018; a broadly transferable solution remains open.
why: One approximation could describe charge localization and static correlation consistently.
key_works: A. J. Cohen, P. Mori-Sánchez and W. Yang (2008), *Insights into current limitations of density functional theory*, [DOI:10.1126/science.1158722](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.1158722); N. Q. Su, C. Li and W. Yang (2018), *Describing strong correlation with fractional-spin correction in density functional theory*, [article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6166809/).

title: Predictive exchange–correlation steps in charge separation
open: Reproduce the spatial steps and derivative discontinuities that enforce correct electron allocation between weakly coupled fragments during dissociation and charge transfer. Predict their positions and heights from the system itself.
status: Recognized for decades. Analytical work in 2025 derived plateaus and investigated approximations; inexpensive general reproduction remains unresolved.
why: Incorrect fractional charge corrupts redox energetics and charge-transfer mechanisms.
key_works: N. E. Rahat and E. Kraisler (2025), *Plateaus in the Potentials of Density-Functional Theory: Analytical Derivation and Useful Approximations*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01771); P. Mori-Sánchez and A. J. Cohen (2014), *The derivative discontinuity of the exchange-correlation functional*, [article](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24920317/).

title: Reliable density-functional double excitations
open: Predict excitation energies, oscillator strengths and potential-energy surfaces for states with substantial double-excitation character across diverse molecules, including state mixing and bond dissociation.
status: Ordinary adiabatic linear-response TDDFT has a longstanding limitation here. A 2025 ensemble-functional construction resolved representative failures; broad validation and reliable dynamics remain open.
why: Double excitations participate in photochemistry, relaxation and multiexciton generation.
key_works: T. Gould, S. G. Dale, L. Kronik and S. Pittalis (2025), *State-Specific Density Functionals for Excited States via a Density-Driven Correlation Model*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.228001](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.228001).

title: Chemically useful tractable classes of the fermion sign problem
