open: Characterize substantial, explicitly defined molecular Hamiltonian families for which unbiased quantum Monte Carlo avoids exponential sign degradation, or prove hardness within those families.
status: Troyer and Wiese established generic sign-problem NP-hardness in 2005. That result leaves the practical tractability boundary for structured molecular families incompletely characterized.
why: A classification would identify when unbiased correlation calculations can scale.
key_works: M. Troyer and U.-J. Wiese (2005), *Computational Complexity and Fundamental Limitations to Fermionic Quantum Monte Carlo Simulations*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.170201).

title: Robust transition-metal spin-state energetics
open: Predict spin-state free energies and equilibrium populations across oxidation states, temperatures and solvents with calibrated uncertainties.
status: Decades old. The 2024 SSE17 comparison found CCSD(T) best among the methods tested, with a mean absolute electronic-energy error of 1.5 kcal/mol.
why: Spin populations control magnetic properties and reaction pathways.
key_works: M. Radoń et al. (2024), *Performance of quantum chemistry methods for a benchmark set of spin-state energetics derived from experimental data of 17 transition metal complexes (SSE17)*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC05471G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC05471G).

title: Experimentally anchored spin-gap benchmark beyond SSE17
open: Establish reference spin splittings for multimetal and heavier-element complexes, with quantified vibrational, environmental and measurement corrections.
status: SSE17 assembled 17 experimentally grounded cases in 2024; broader chemical coverage remains incomplete.
why: Uncertain references obscure genuine computational improvements.
key_works: M. Radoń et al. (2024), *Performance of quantum chemistry methods for a benchmark set of spin-state energetics derived from experimental data of 17 transition metal complexes (SSE17)*, [DOI:10.1039/D4SC05471G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4SC05471G).

title: Certified control of fixed-node bias
open: Obtain usable bounds on fixed-node energy errors for complex molecules, or a demonstrably convergent procedure reducing them to a prescribed tolerance.
status: Fixed-node diffusion Monte Carlo has been powerful for decades, but nodal bias remains difficult to certify. Neural trial wavefunctions improved molecular calculations in 2023; small sampling errors do not certify small nodal errors.
why: Certification would make numerical predictions quantitatively trustworthy.
key_works: W. Ren, W. Fu, X. Wu and J. Chen (2023), *Towards the ground state of molecules via diffusion Monte Carlo on neural networks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-37609-3); [arXiv:2204.13903](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.13903).

title: Wavefunction foundation models across chemical regimes
open: Transfer pretrained electronic wavefunctions to unfamiliar elements, charges, geometries and correlation regimes with reliable accuracy diagnostics and limited retraining. Validate forces and energy differences.
status: Orbformer, first posted in 2025 and revised in September 2026, learned from 22,000 structures and reported chemical accuracy on selected bond-breaking benchmarks. Broad reliability under distribution shift remains open.
why: Reusing electronic knowledge could substantially reduce repeated wavefunction optimization.
key_works: A. Foster et al. (2025/2026), *An ab initio foundation model of wavefunctions that accurately describes chemical bond breaking*, [arXiv:2506.19960](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.19960), DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-76604-2.

title: Ground-state preparation with predictable chemical scaling
open: Prepare states for quantum energy estimation on difficult chemical instances with favorable total cost and success probability as system size grows. Assess overlap or energy distributions without assuming the exact answer is known.
status: Fomichev and colleagues supplied an integrated preparation and energy-distribution framework in 2024; inexpensive preparation across strongly correlated molecular families remains unestablished.
why: State preparation can dominate the cost of otherwise efficient quantum algorithms.
key_works: S. Fomichev et al. (2024), *Initial State Preparation for Quantum Chemistry on Quantum Computers*, [DOI:10.1103/PRXQuantum.5.040339](https://doi.org/10.1103/PRXQuantum.5.040339); [arXiv:2310.18410](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.18410).

title: End-to-end useful quantum advantage for molecular energies
open: Demonstrate a consequential molecular-energy calculation outperforming the best applicable classical methods after including preparation, error correction, measurements and model errors.
status: A 2026 preprint estimated selected 20–50-orbital calculations on roughly 100,000 physical qubits. These are architecture-dependent resource estimates; the requested experimental advantage remains open.
why: It would establish when quantum computing changes the practical cost of chemical discovery.
key_works: S. Kanasugi, R. Toshio, K. Maruyama and H. Oshima (2026), *Enabling Chemically Accurate Quantum Phase Estimation in the Early Fault-Tolerant Regime*, [arXiv:2603.22778](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.22778), preprint.

title: Affordable coupled electron–nuclear quantum dynamics
open: Simulate chemically useful real-time motion with electrons and nuclei both treated quantum mechanically, controlling spatial discretization, pseudopotential and readout errors.
status: A 2025 proposal estimated 808 logical qubits and approximately \(10^{11}\) Toffoli gates per femtosecond for an ammonia–boron-trifluoride example. Affordable implementation remains a substantial gap.
why: It would address reactions where electronic transitions and nuclear tunneling are inseparable.
key_works: F. H. da Jornada et al. (2025), *A comprehensive framework to simulate real-time chemical dynamics on a fault-tolerant quantum computer*, [arXiv:2504.06348](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.06348), preprint.

title: Uniformly reliable surface hopping
open: Develop an affordable trajectory method treating coherence, decoherence, state crossings and equilibrium populations consistently across coupling regimes, with controlled errors against quantum dynamics.
status: Surface hopping has developed over decades. Mannouch and Richardson’s 2023 mapping approach supplied a principled alternative, while general reliability for realistic multistate dynamics remains unresolved.
why: Photochemical branching depends on electronic transitions and nuclear motion evolving together.
key_works: J. R. Mannouch and J. O. Richardson (2023), *A mapping approach to surface hopping*, [arXiv:2212.11773](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.11773).

title: Common molecular benchmarks for nonadiabatic dynamics
open: Build public benchmarks with shared initial conditions, reproducible Hamiltonians, converged reference observables, experimental comparisons and quantified uncertainties.
status: A 2024 CECAM workshop and 2025 community roadmap explicitly identified the shortage of comprehensive realistic benchmarks. Individual comparisons provide partial coverage.
why: Consistent references would make algorithm selection and claims of progress assessable.
key_works: L. E. Cigrang et al. (2025), *Roadmap for Molecular Benchmarks in Nonadiabatic Dynamics*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpca.5c02171](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.5c02171); [arXiv:2502.14569](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.14569).

title: Predictive roaming-channel branching
open: Predict roaming-reaction branching fractions, lifetimes and correlated product states across excitation energies and isotopes. Determine when quantum resonances invalidate classical trajectory descriptions.
status: Roaming was identified in formaldehyde in 2004. Direct observation of a roaming intermediate in 2024 strengthened mechanistic evidence; transferable quantitative rate theory remains open.
why: Roaming changes combustion and photolysis products without following a conventional transition-state pathway.
key_works: G. L. Abma et al. (2024), *Direct Observation of a Roaming Intermediate and Its Dynamics*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.4c01543](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.4c01543).

title: Complete state-to-state polyatomic reaction maps
open: Measure and predict correlated quantum-state distributions of all products, including dependence on selected reactant vibrations and collision geometry. Quantify undetected channels.
status: State-resolved work extends beyond triatomics, but comprehensive coverage remains limited. A 2025 D + CH₄ study identified umbrella bending as a reporter of reaction dynamics.
why: Such maps reveal how energy placed in a particular mode controls outcomes.
key_works: H. Pan et al. (2023), *State-to-State Dynamics in Mode-Selective Polyatomic Reactions*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.3c02853](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.3c02853); Y. Tan et al. (2025), *Revealing umbrella bending as a reporter mode in the D+CH4 reaction*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-61117-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61117-1).

title: Molecular parity-violating enantiomer energy difference
open: Measure the electroweak energy or transition-frequency difference between molecular enantiomers with systematic errors below the predicted signal.
status: Predicted for decades. A July 2026 proposal still describes molecular parity violation as experimentally undetected; heavy chiral species and ultracold amplification provide possible routes.
why: It would test the weak interaction in molecular matter and constrain microscopic sources of chiral bias.
key_works: D. Martínez-Gil, P. Bargueño and S. Miret-Artés (2026), *Ultracold amplification proposal for parity violation in chiral molecules*, [DOI:10.1103/54yp-6397](https://doi.org/10.1103/54yp-6397); [arXiv:2606.08717](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.08717).

title: Quantum tomography of a reacting polyatomic molecule
open: Reconstruct an experimentally defensible molecular density matrix during reaction, including relevant coherences. State identifiability assumptions and quantify missing information.
status: A 2021 diffraction experiment reconstructed rotational wavepackets. Extending tomography to coupled electronic and vibrational motion in reacting polyatomics remains substantially harder.
why: Quantum-state information can distinguish mechanisms producing similar average structures.
key_works: M. Zhang et al. (2021), *Quantum state tomography of molecules by ultrafast diffraction*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-021-25770-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-021-25770-6).

title: Entanglement-assisted selection of bimolecular products
open: Experimentally control product-state branching by deliberately entangling reactants, and distinguish the advantage from ordinary reactant-state preparation.
status: A 2025 calculation predicted complete control of product rotational parity for an ultracold KRb + KRb example. Experimental implementation and generalization remain open.
why: Entanglement could become an independent resource for chemical selectivity.
key_works: A. Devolder, T. Tscherbul and P. Brumer (2025), *Leveraging Reactant Entanglement in the Coherent Control of Ultracold Bimolecular Chemical Reactions*, [DOI:10.1103/7c2n-xkpg](https://doi.org/10.1103/7c2n-xkpg); [arXiv:2505.10684](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.10684).

title: Separating collective vibrational-cavity effects from heat transport
open: Determine which rate changes require collective quantum light–matter effects after independently measuring temperature, radiative energy transfer and surface chemistry. Predict residual effects quantitatively.
status: The field expanded after 2015. Brawley and colleagues showed in 2025 that radiative energy transfer explains a particular dehydration effect; other systems remain unsettled.
why: Mechanistic discrimination is necessary for predictable cavity-controlled chemistry.
key_works: Z. T. Brawley et al. (2025), *Vibrational weak and strong coupling modify a chemical reaction via cavity-mediated radiative energy transfer*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-024-01723-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-024-01723-6).

title: Test of the vibrational-condensation hypothesis
open: Determine whether macroscopic occupation of a collective vibrational state occurs under experimental dark-cavity conditions and quantitatively explains observed chemical changes.
status: Mondal, Montillo Vega and Huo proposed this mechanism in July 2026. It remains a theoretical hypothesis requiring discriminating experimental tests.
why: Validation could connect molecular coupling to macroscopic reaction-rate changes.
key_works: M. E. Mondal, S. Montillo Vega and P. Huo (2026), *A macroscopic condensation theory for vibrational strong coupling effects*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75222-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75222-2).

title: Quantitative map of water’s liquid–liquid critical region
open: Independently determine the coexistence curve, critical parameters and scaling behavior of deeply supercooled water while separating equilibration from crystallization.
status: You and colleagues reported experimental evidence for a liquid–liquid critical point in March 2026, including critical-region behavior around 210 ± 8 K. Independent quantitative phase mapping remains open.
why: It would constrain explanations of water’s thermodynamic and structural anomalies.
key_works: S. You et al. (2026), *Experimental evidence of a liquid-liquid critical point in supercooled water*, [DOI:10.1126/science.aec0018](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aec0018).

title: Isotope shifts of water’s liquid–liquid transition
open: Determine H₂O–D₂O shifts in liquid–liquid coexistence and critical parameters experimentally, and predict them with controlled electronic and nuclear quantum errors.
status: Path-integral calculations, including a 2026 equation-of-state study, quantify shifts within specific models. A model-independent experimental phase diagram for both isotopes remains absent.
why: Isotope effects can separate nuclear quantum contributions from classical network mechanisms.
key_works: A. Eltareb et al. (2026), *Nuclear Quantum Effects on the Equation of State of Water: Insights from the Potential Energy Landscape Formalism*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c02151).

title: Controlled real-time nuclear quantum dynamics in liquids
open: Obtain scalable real-time correlation functions and reaction dynamics with controlled errors for quantum nuclei in condensed phases. Establish failure boundaries for tunneling, coherence and spectral line shapes.
status: Equilibrium path integrals are established; real-time dynamics remains harder. DL_POLY Quantum 2.1 incorporated improved centroid and quasi-centroid methods in 2025, with selected spectral demonstrations.
why: Quantum hydrogen motion affects reaction rates, spectra and transport.
key_works: N. London et al. (2025), *DL_POLY Quantum 2.1: A Suite of Real-Time Path Integral Methods for the Simulation of Dynamical Properties and Vibrational Spectra*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpca.4c08644](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.4c08644).

title: Convention-consistent single-ion hydration energetics
open: Reconcile calculated and experimentally inferred single-ion hydration free energies under shared surface-potential and electrochemical conventions, with quantified electronic, finite-size and interfacial errors.
status: Debated for decades. Quantum simulations provide operationally defined scales, including the 2017 study below; broad transferable accuracy remains incomplete. A convention-free absolute single-ion number is not a physically appropriate target.
why: Ion energetics underpin acidity, solubility and electrochemical interfaces.
key_works: T. T. Duignan, M. D. Baer, G. K. Schenter and C. J. Mundy (2017), *Real single ion solvation free energies with quantum mechanical simulation*, [DOI:10.1039/C7SC02138K](https://doi.org/10.1039/C7SC02138K).

title: Depth-resolved self-ion distribution at the air–water interface
open: Measure hydronium and hydroxide concentration profiles across uncontaminated, nominally neutral water surfaces with molecular depth resolution, reconciling spectroscopy, electrokinetics and simulation.
status: The interface’s acid–base character has been disputed for decades. A 2024 simulation proposed separate hydronium and hydroxide layers; direct confirmation remains open.
why: Local proton availability controls interfacial reaction pathways.
key_works: P. Zhang, M. Feng and X. Xu (2024), *Double-Layer Distribution of Hydronium and Hydroxide Ions in the Air–Water Interface*, [DOI:10.1021/acsphyschemau.3c00076](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsphyschemau.3c00076).

title: Surface dependence of anomalous electrolyte underscreening
open: Determine when long force-decay lengths in concentrated electrolytes reflect bulk screening, clustering or surface-specific effects. Predict concentration and substrate dependence consistently across measurement methods.
status: Positive and null observations coexist. A 2025 simulation connected long-ranged forces to solvent-induced clusters but did not reproduce the full concentration dependence.
why: Screening models determine predictions of colloidal stability and interfacial ion organization.
key_works: D. Ribar, C. E. Woodward and J. Forsman (2025), *Solvent-induced ion clusters generate long-ranged double-layer forces at high ionic strengths*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SM00027K](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SM00027K).

title: Finite-temperature ideal glass transition in molecular liquids
open: Establish whether realistic three-dimensional molecular liquids possess an equilibrium ideal-glass transition with vanishing configurational entropy, or determine what avoids it.
status: The entropy-crisis question dates to Kauzmann’s 1948 analysis. Enhanced sampling has extended equilibrium entropy measurements, but extrapolation to a genuine singularity remains disputed.
why: It would distinguish major explanations of glass formation.
key_works: L. Berthier et al. (2017), *Configurational entropy measurements in extremely supercooled liquids that break the glass ceiling*, [arXiv:1704.08257](https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.08257).

title: Molecular origin of secondary glass relaxation
open: Predict the motions responsible for secondary relaxation peaks and excess wings, and their coupling to structural relaxation across chemically distinct glass formers.
status: These longstanding spectroscopic features are becoming accessible to simulations. Simon, Barrat and Berthier reached experimental-glass-transition conditions for a molecular model in 2026 and visualized excess-wing motion.
why: Secondary relaxation governs dielectric loss, mechanical response and residual mobility.
key_works: R. Simon, J.-L. Barrat and L. Berthier (2026), *Molecular Motion at the Experimental Glass Transition*, [DOI:10.1103/4twk-33j7](https://doi.org/10.1103/4twk-33j7).

title: Hydrophobic attraction for heterogeneous molecular surfaces
open: Predict water-mediated association free energies for chemically patterned, curved and flexible surfaces from measurable properties. Establish when critical-drying descriptions remain quantitative.
status: A universal molecular description has remained elusive for decades. Wilding and Turci’s 2025 theory explains temperature-dependent attraction for model spherical solutes; heterogeneous real surfaces remain open.
why: It would improve predictive self-assembly and recognition models.
key_works: N. B. Wilding and F. Turci (2025), *Origin of the inverse temperature dependence of hydrophobic attraction*, [DOI:10.1103/66lz-1yw9](https://doi.org/10.1103/66lz-1yw9).

title: Operational electric-field distributions at reactive aqueous surfaces
open: Determine local electric-field distributions and lifetimes experienced by reacting interfacial solutes, with consistent mappings between spectroscopy and simulations. Test their quantitative contribution to rate changes.
status: A 2025 study found no exceptionally strong or long-lived fields at pristine neutral air–water interfaces. Charged and compositionally complex reactive interfaces require separate measurements.
why: It would replace qualitative field explanations with constrained reaction models.
key_works: J. C. Shirley et al. (2025), *Reevaluating Anomalous Electric Fields at the Air–Water Interface: A Surface-Specific Spectroscopic Survey*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c14541](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c14541); [arXiv:2508.15422](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.15422).

title: Transferable homogeneous ice-nucleation rates
open: Predict ice-nucleation rates across temperature, droplet size and cooling history with uncertainties covering microscopic models and measurement protocols.
status: Studied for decades. A 2024 analysis showed that droplet-size dispersion biases inferred barriers and supplied an improved analysis framework; transferable microscopic prediction remains open.
why: Ice-formation rates control clouds, cryopreservation and industrial freezing.
key_works: R. K. R. Addula, I. de Almeida Ribeiro, V. Molinero and B. Peters (2024), *Modeling homogeneous ice nucleation from drop-freezing experiments: impact of droplet volume dispersion and cooling rates*, [DOI:10.5194/acp-24-10833-2024](https://doi.org/10.5194/acp-24-10833-2024).

title: Complete structure searches for flexible molecular crystals
open: Generate all experimentally relevant low-free-energy packings of flexible molecules, salts and coordination compounds, with meaningful search-completeness diagnostics.
status: The seventh blind test, reported in 2024, showed stronger performance for simple targets than complex systems; two groups first blindly predicted disorder.
why: Energy ranking cannot recover a relevant structure that was never generated.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Predicting cocrystal stoichiometry and competing phases
open: Predict cocrystal stoichiometries and competition with separate crystals, salts, solvates and disordered phases. Validate composition-dependent phase diagrams.
status: The 2024 seventh blind test explored stoichiometry prediction and found promising approaches; a generally reliable joint composition-and-structure predictor remains open.
why: Stoichiometry determines material properties and synthetic accessibility.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure generation methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624007492](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624007492).

title: Reliable polymorph stability ranking at ambient conditions
open: Rank closely competing molecular-crystal free energies with errors below their separations, including thermal, quantum and disorder effects.
status: In the 2024 seventh blind test, dispersion-corrected periodic DFT often agreed with experiment, but thermal corrections helped only some targets and calculations remained costly.
why: Stability ordering determines solid-form conversion and shelf-life risks.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679).

title: Predicted missing stable polymorph of blind-test target XXXII
open: Produce and characterize the predicted lower-free-energy form of target XXXII, or establish why its predicted stability or accessibility fails.
status: Several 2024 blind-test methods placed observed forms over 4 kJ/mol above predicted minima. A 2025 study still identified the missing global minimum.
why: It is a concrete test of computational discovery of hidden solid forms.
key_works: L. M. Hunnisett et al. (2024), *The seventh blind test of crystal structure prediction: structure ranking methods*, [DOI:10.1107/S2052520624008679](https://doi.org/10.1107/S2052520624008679); J. van de Streek et al. (2025), *A Conceptual Framework for the Crystallizability of Organic Compounds*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c08933](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c08933).

title: Affordable anharmonic lattice free energies
open: Compute converged anharmonic free-energy differences for large libraries of flexible and disordered molecular polymorphs, including finite-size errors, at practical cost.
status: Normalizing-flow calculations gave accurate free energies for two modeled ice polymorphs in 2025. Diverse molecular crystals remain a broader transfer and scaling challenge.
why: Anharmonic entropy can reverse polymorph stability rankings.
key_works: E. Olehnovics et al. (2025), *Accurate Lattice Free Energies of Packing Polymorphs from Probabilistic Generative Models*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01612).

title: Absolute nucleation-rate prediction across solvents
open: Predict absolute nucleation rates and induction-time distributions across solvents, supersaturations and impurities, including desolvation and interfacial barriers.
status: A 2025 study connected computed activity coefficients with relative nucleation difficulty for three organic solutes. Universal absolute rates and polymorph branching remain unresolved.
why: It would reduce empirical crystallization development.
key_works: J. Zeglinski et al. (2025), *Toward Predicting Nucleation Difficulty of Organic Compounds Crystallized from Different Solvents*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.cgd.5c00176](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.cgd.5c00176).

title: Methane-hydrate nucleation under realistic interfaces
open: Predict hydrate pathways and induction times across realistic methane concentrations, sediments, ice surfaces and thermal histories.
status: A 2025 study quantified ice-mediated acceleration with 200 trajectories at one temperature, pressure and concentration. Generalization from such controlled simulations remains open.
why: Predictive kinetics matter for gas storage, pipelines and seafloor processes.
key_works: D. Kumar, L.-Y. Huang, D. T. Wu and S.-T. Lin (2025), *Accelerated Methane Hydrate Nucleation near Ice: Free Energy Landscape and Kinetic Enhancement*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpcc.5c03969](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpcc.5c03969).

title: Predicting which computed polymorphs can actually crystallize
open: Given a crystal landscape and processing conditions, identify accessible minima and synthetic routes, including solvent-dependent strain and nucleation-surface costs.
status: A 2025 crystallizability framework linked molecular strain with accessibility but identified missing absolute, solvent-dependent nucleation criteria.
why: Predicted thermodynamic stability is useful only when the material can be obtained.
key_works: J. van de Streek et al. (2025), *A Conceptual Framework for the Crystallizability of Organic Compounds*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c08933](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c08933).

title: Carrier of the 5780 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Identify the carrier through laboratory spectra matching the astronomical wavelength, profile and companion transitions, with a plausible abundance.
status: Unidentified since Heger’s 1922 report. A 2025 quantum-chemical study rejected several proposed molecular families through incompatible spectra.
why: Identification would turn a widespread absorption feature into a chemical diagnostic.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Carrier of the 5797 Å diffuse interstellar band
open: Assign this band’s carrier and reproduce its spectrum and environmental dependence independently of the 5780 Å assignment.
status: Open since 1922. Correlated band families and candidate calculations constrain possibilities; a confirmed molecular assignment remains lacking.
why: It would identify a chemically informative component of interstellar matter.
key_works: H. Seuret et al. (2025), *Vetting molecular candidates posited for the first diffuse interstellar bands (5780 and 5797 Å): a quantum chemical study*, [DOI:10.1039/D4CP04023F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D4CP04023F).

title: Missing interstellar oxygen reservoir
open: Locate and quantify oxygen absent from observed gas, silicates and conventional ice inventories in translucent and dense clouds, closing the abundance budget with diagnostic spectra.
status: A longstanding depletion discrepancy persists. A 2025 analysis identifies far-infrared signatures of large icy grains as a discriminating observation.
why: Oxygen partition constrains planet-forming materials and water delivery.
key_works: T. Onaka, I. Sakon, T. Shimonishi and M. Honda (2025), *Searching for missing interstellar oxygen in the far-infrared*, [arXiv:2509.01846](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.01846).

title: Dense-cloud sulfur budget and phase partition
open: Quantify sulfur partition among gas, salts, polysulfanes, elemental sulfur and refractory grains in the same sightlines, explaining depletion through cloud evolution.
status: The decades-old budget problem has plausible candidates: 2025 experiments produced polysulfanes and S₈ in irradiated ice. XRISM iron-sulfide evidence from other sightlines does not close every dense-cloud budget.
why: The reservoir’s volatility determines sulfur delivery to planets.
key_works: A. Herath et al. (2025), *Missing interstellar sulfur in inventories of polysulfanes and molecular octasulfur crowns*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-61259-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61259-2); L. Corrales et al. (2025), *XRISM insights for interstellar sulfur*, [DOI:10.1093/pasj/psaf068](https://doi.org/10.1093/pasj/psaf068).

title: Cold-cloud formation or survival of pyrene
open: Determine whether pyrene in TMC-1 forms locally at low temperature or survives transport from warmer regions, reproducing abundances and nitrile-isomer ratios with constrained kinetics.
status: Cyanopyrene detections in 2024–2025 established four-ring aromatic chemistry in a cold cloud. The parent aromatic inventory’s origin remains unresolved.
why: It tests how large carbon molecules arise before star formation.
key_works: G. Wenzel et al. (2024), *Detection of interstellar 1-cyanopyrene: A four-ring polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adq6391](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adq6391); G. Wenzel et al. (2025), *Detections of interstellar aromatic nitriles 2-cyanopyrene and 4-cyanopyrene in TMC-1*, [DOI:10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41550-024-02410-9).

title: Interstellar enantiomeric excess
open: Measure a nonzero enantiomeric excess, or a useful upper bound, for an interstellar chiral molecule using handedness-sensitive observations with controlled polarization errors.
status: Propylene oxide was detected in 2016, establishing identity without measuring handedness. Meteorite measurements concern different samples and histories.
why: It would constrain astronomical contributions to biological handedness.
key_works: B. A. McGuire et al. (2016), *Discovery of the interstellar chiral molecule propylene oxide (CH3CHCH2O)*, [arXiv:1606.07483](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.07483).

title: Distribution-resolved diffusion data for interstellar ices
open: Measure diffusion-barrier distributions for atoms and radicals on realistic evolving amorphous ices, with morphology dependence and uncertainties suitable for reaction networks.
status: Grain-surface models have used incomplete inputs for decades. A 2025 assessment identifies low-temperature mobility and restructuring as continuing gaps.
why: Encounter rates determine whether complex molecules form before desorption or destruction.
key_works: N. F. W. Ligterink et al. (2025), *Molecular mobility of extraterrestrial ices: surface diffusion in astrochemistry and planetary science*, [DOI:10.1039/D5CP02278A](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5CP02278A).

title: Interstellar phosphorus inventory and controlling reactions
open: Determine gas/grain phosphorus partition and measure reactions controlling PO and PN abundances, separating depletion assumptions from kinetic explanations.
status: Observations constrain only part of the inventory. A 2025 sensitivity analysis reduced a 14-rate model to three influential parameters, identifying valuable measurement targets.
why: It constrains chemically available phosphorus supplied to forming planets.
key_works: M. Fernández-Ruz et al. (2025), *Strong parameter hierarchy in the interstellar phosphorus chemical network*, [DOI:10.3389/fspas.2025.1570525](https://doi.org/10.3389/fspas.2025.1570525).

title: Synthesis and identification of element 119
open: Produce nuclei with atomic number 119 and establish their identity through reproducible decay or mass evidence.
status: Still a search target in the 2026 experimental review. A 2022 barrier measurement constrained reaction energies for ⁵¹V + ²⁴⁸Cm without establishing synthesis.
why: It would open the eighth period and test nuclear stability and relativistic periodicity.
key_works: M. Tanaka et al. (2022), *Probing Optimal Reaction Energy for Synthesis of Element 119 from 51V+248Cm Reaction with Quasielastic Barrier Distribution Measurement*, [DOI:10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201](https://doi.org/10.7566/JPSJ.91.084201); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Synthesis and identification of element 120
open: Produce and identify element 120 with decay assignments and reaction evidence sufficient for independent confirmation.
status: Searches remain underway in the 2026 review. Livermorium production using a ⁵⁰Ti beam in 2024 demonstrated precursor technology.
why: It tests shell stabilization and extends experimentally known periodicity.
key_works: J. M. Gates et al. (2024), *Toward the Discovery of New Elements: Production of Livermorium (Z=116) with 50Ti*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.133.172502); J. M. Gates and J. L. Pore (2026), *The Quest for Superheavy Nuclei: An Experimental Perspective*, [DOI:10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404](https://doi.org/10.1146/annurev-nucl-100324-103404).

title: Experimental chemical properties of oganesson
open: Measure an oganesson chemical or response property, such as adsorption, polarizability or molecular binding, to test relativistic predictions.
status: Individual nuclei exist, while chemical behavior remains computationally inferred. A 2020 calculation predicted major departures from lighter noble gases; atom scarcity and short lifetimes obstruct experiments.
why: Oganesson is an extreme test of the basis of periodic trends.
key_works: O. R. Smits et al. (2020), *Oganesson: A Noble Gas Element That Is Neither Noble Nor a Gas*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202011976](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202011976).

title: Operationally predictive actinide covalency
open: Connect specified spectroscopic observables and orbital descriptions to transferable predictions of actinide bonding and reactivity, resolving differences between overlap-based and energy-matching interpretations.
status: Longstanding ambiguity has become experimentally sharper. In 2025, resonant inelastic X-ray scattering probed 5f populations and covalency without establishing a universal predictive descriptor.
why: Reliable bonding models support selective actinide coordination and separation.
key_works: B. Schacherl et al. (2025), *Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering tools to count 5 f electrons of actinides and probe bond covalency*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-54574-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-54574-7).

title: Chemically reproducible thorium-229 nuclear clocks
open: Control host composition, dopant sites and defects so independently prepared solid-state nuclear clocks agree with smaller, fully budgeted systematic uncertainties.
status: Ooi and colleagues measured 220 Hz reproducibility, approximately \(1.1\times10^{-13}\) fractionally, across two differently doped CaF₂ crystals in 2026. Their temperature-insensitive operating point addresses one variation source.
why: Reproducible host chemistry is necessary for deployable nuclear frequency standards.
key_works: T. Ooi et al. (2026), *Frequency reproducibility of solid-state thorium-229 nuclear clocks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09999-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09999-5).

title: Defect-controlled thorium isomer quenching
open: Engineer host defects allowing efficient, switchable nuclear-state readout or reset while preserving coherence and frequency stability during interrogation.
status: Photoinduced quenching was demonstrated in 2025. Defect-mediated internal conversion explains observations, but reproducible materials design with quantified clock tradeoffs remains open.
why: Controlled reset could shorten measurement cycles and improve detection.
key_works: J. E. S. Terhune et al. (2025), *Photoinduced quenching of the 229Th isomer in a solid-state host*, [DOI:10.1103/glzr-thyw](https://doi.org/10.1103/glzr-thyw).

title: Closed-loop, energy-competitive lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis
open: Close electrolyte, proton-carrier and lithium balances during continuous ammonia production from nitrogen and hydrogen, at total energy cost competitive with renewable-hydrogen Haber–Bosch.
status: A longstanding efficiency and scale problem. Li et al. demonstrated 300 hours in a 25 cm² flow electrolyser in 2024; Faradaic efficiency alone does not establish total energy competitiveness.
why: Enables distributed fertilizer production with recyclable process materials.
key_works: S. Li et al. (2024), *Long-term continuous ammonia electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07276-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-024-07276-5).

title: Predictive solid-electrolyte interphases for nitrogen reduction
open: Predict ammonia selectivity and aging across electrolyte compositions and current histories from independently measured interphase chemistry and transport.
status: Mechanistic understanding is developing. Herzog et al. resolved ethanol-driven lithium-alkoxide formation and interphase–conversion correlations in 2026; transferable prediction remains open.
why: It would turn empirical electrolyte screening into systematic design.
key_works: A. Herzog et al. (2026), *Unveiling solid electrolyte interphase dynamics in electrochemical lithium-mediated ammonia synthesis via operando Raman spectroscopy*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01562-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01562-3).

title: Productive direct aqueous dinitrogen electroreduction
open: Demonstrate reproducible net conversion of purified N₂ to ammonia in water at useful rates and selectivity, with isotope tracing, complete nitrogen balances and independent replication.
status: Pursued for decades; contamination remains decisive. Schneider et al. found in 2025 that reported Fe/Zn–N–C activity disappeared when nitrogen-oxide contamination was excluded.
why: It could simplify ammonia electrosynthesis by eliminating reactive-metal mediation.
key_works: C. Schneider et al. (2025), *Reevaluating the Activity of ZIF-8 Based FeNCs for Electrochemical Ammonia Production*, [primary institutional record](https://www.materials.ox.ac.uk/publication/2352947/ora-hyrax).

title: Sacrificial-reagent-free molecular photofixation of nitrogen
open: Couple molecular nitrogen reduction to water oxidation so light, nitrogen and water are the only net inputs and ammonia and oxygen the net products.
status: Molecular fixation has advanced since the early 2000s. Yamazaki et al. achieved visible-light ammonia formation with water in 2025, while tertiary phosphines supplied sacrificial reducing equivalents.
why: It would establish a materially closed artificial photosynthetic ammonia cycle.
key_works: Y. Yamazaki, Y. Endo and Y. Nishibayashi (2025), *Catalytic ammonia formation from dinitrogen, water, and visible light energy*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-59727-w).

title: Sustainable calcium-mediated nitrogen reduction
open: Build a continuously regenerating calcium-mediated ammonia reactor with controlled passivation and no net destruction of electrolyte or proton donor.
status: Fu et al. established calcium-mediated electrosynthesis in work published online in 2023 and in a 2024 issue. Durable closed-loop operation remains unresolved.
why: It tests whether an abundant mediator can replace lithium while preserving selectivity.
key_works: X. Fu et al. (2024), *Calcium-mediated nitrogen reduction for electrochemical ammonia synthesis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41563-023-01702-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-023-01702-1).

title: Energy-efficient plasma–electrochemical nitrogen fixation
open: Optimize the complete air-to-NOₓ-to-ammonia chain, including plasma, absorption, electroreduction and recovery, to outperform competing distributed routes under consistent energy accounting.
status: A 2025 four-cell demonstration exceeded 91% ammonia Faradaic efficiency and 95% NOₓ conversion, with over 200 hours of electrolyser stability. Integrated energy competitiveness remains open.
why: It could enable small fertilizer plants responsive to renewable electricity.
key_works: W. Liu et al. (2025), *Full runner electrolyzer stack for industrial-current-density NOx−-mediated ammonia synthesis from air and water*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-61069-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-61069-6).

title: Vacancy catalysts for practical low-pressure ammonia synthesis
open: Maintain active anion vacancies during prolonged nitrogen–hydrogen conversion and transient operation, with useful production rates and abundant catalyst constituents.
status: Mild-condition alternatives to Haber–Bosch have been sought for a century. A 2025 study demonstrated nitrogen activation on Ba–Si oxynitride-hydride vacancies.
why: Lower pressure and broader catalyst choices could support smaller ammonia plants.
key_works: Z. Zhang et al. (2025), *Anion vacancies activate N2 to ammonia on Ba–Si orthosilicate oxynitride-hydride*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01737-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01737-8).

title: Low-temperature, precious-metal-free ammonia cracking
open: Combine high conversion, very low residual ammonia and sustained hydrogen productivity using inexpensive catalysts, counting all thermal or optical input.
status: A longstanding hydrogen-carrier bottleneck. Ni–CeO₂−x photothermal interfaces operated for over 50 hours in a 2025 demonstration; long-duration product-purity performance remains unresolved.
why: It would provide fuel-cell-grade hydrogen from ammonia at lower material and heating cost.
key_works: R. Tan et al. (2025), *Breakthrough photothermal ammonia decomposition via low-barrier Ni-CeO2-x interfaces on carbon nanotubes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-66325-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-66325-3).

title: Direct methane-to-methanol with simultaneous selectivity and throughput
open: Sustain direct methane oxidation to recoverable methanol at substantial conversion, suppressing overoxidation and accounting for oxidant and energy inputs.
status: A decades-old problem. Li et al. achieved 83.5% methanol selectivity through time-dependent charge control in 2026; continuous high-conversion manufacture remains a separate target.
why: It could create smaller routes from methane to transportable liquid feedstocks.
key_works: Y. Li et al. (2026), *Spatiotemporal photon distribution control on active sites enables bio-inspired methane-to-methanol conversion*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-70134-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70134-7).

title: Abundant-metal electrochemical methane hydroxylation
open: Achieve selective room-temperature methane-to-methanol electrooxidation on an abundant-metal anode, with sustained product accumulation and verified regeneration of the oxygen source.
status: Kim et al. demonstrated carbonate-promoted IrO₂ oxidation in 2025, including approximately 11.1 mmol methanol g-catalyst⁻¹ h⁻¹ during continuous operation. Abundant-metal replacement remains open.
why: It would reduce resource constraints on electrically controlled methane activation.
key_works: C. Kim et al. (2025), *High-selectivity room-temperature partial oxidation of methane to methanol enabled by electrochemical oxygen promotion on IrO2 catalysts*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01363-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01363-0).

title: High-yield oxidative methane coupling without deep oxidation
open: Combine substantial single-pass methane conversion, high C₂ selectivity, sustained catalyst activity and low heating or photon input.
status: Pursued since the 1980s. Song et al. reported approximately 90% C₂+ selectivity and high photocatalytic productivity in 2025; the combined conversion–selectivity–energy target remains open.
why: It could provide alternative routes to basic petrochemicals.
key_works: H. Song et al. (2025), *Integrating photochemical and photothermal effects for selective oxidative coupling of methane into C2+ hydrocarbons with multiple active sites*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-58101-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58101-0).

title: Coke-resistant nonoxidative methane aromatization
open: Sustain methane-to-aromatics conversion while preventing persistent coke formation and avoiding frequent regeneration that damages the catalyst.
status: A decades-old challenge. A 2024 Pt–Bi/Mo/ZSM-5 study reported 18.7% methane conversion and 69.4% benzene selectivity; lifetime and joint performance remain limiting.
why: It would co-produce aromatic feedstocks and hydrogen directly from methane.
key_works: W. Bian et al. (2024), *Direct conversion of methane to aromatics and hydrogen via a heterogeneous trimetallic synergistic catalyst*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-47595-9).

title: Durable CO₂-rich methane reforming with complete energy accounting
open: Convert CO₂-rich methane streams to specified syngas compositions while controlling carbon deposition and preserving integrated electrochemical–thermal efficiency.
status: Dry reforming has long faced durability problems. Lv et al. demonstrated tandem electro-thermocatalytic super-dry reforming in 2025; integrated lifetime and scale remain open.
why: It would broaden usable gas feeds and support flexible synthesis-gas production.
key_works: H. Lv et al. (2025), *Super-dry reforming of methane using a tandem electro-thermocatalytic system*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01768-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01768-1).

title: Predictive plasma–surface coupling in CO₂ hydrogenation
open: Predict methanol rates and selectivity from plasma excitation, surface state and temperature, quantitatively separating nonequilibrium excitation from heating and mass transfer.
status: A 2026 operando study resolved site evolution and cooperative plasma effects for Cu–Zn/ZSM-5. Transferable mechanistic prediction remains developing.
why: It would enable reliable scale-up of electrically driven catalytic reactors.
key_works: S. Xu et al. (2026), *Unveiling active sites and the cooperative role of non-thermal plasma and copper–zinc catalysts in the hydrogenation of CO2 to methanol*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01477-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01477-5).

title: Atom-resolved catalytic turnover assignments under operating conditions
open: Assign individual turnovers to evolving surface motifs under realistic pressures, quantifying observation-induced changes and rare active sites.
status: Active-site debates date to early heterogeneous catalysis. September 2026 work tracked individual Pt atoms operando and observed coexisting site classes; complete turnover attribution remains harder.
why: It would identify which structures actually perform catalysis during operation.
key_works: K. Jenkinson et al. (2026), *Operando single-atom tracking in individual Pt nanoparticles detects the coexistence of Langmuir and Taylor active sites*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01612-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01612-w).

title: Catalysis by complete fluxional cluster ensembles
open: Predict activity and selectivity from populated, interconverting cluster ensembles and validate the contributions of individual ensemble members experimentally.
status: Fluxionality has complicated cluster catalysis for decades. A 2025 multiscale study showed collective contributions across sizes, isomers and sites; transferable experimental validation remains incomplete.
why: Catalyst design must account for structures populated under working conditions.
key_works: J.-L. Chen et al. (2025), *Collectivity effect in cluster catalysis under operational conditions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-64187-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-64187-3).

title: Low-voltage acidic CO₂-to-ethylene electrolysis at scale
open: Maintain selective C–C coupling in practical-area acid-fed electrolysers while jointly reducing full-cell voltage, hydrogen evolution and degradation.
status: A 2025 demonstration achieved 10 A operation for over 300 hours, approximately 50% ethylene Faradaic efficiency and about 4.5 V. Efficient long-life manufacture remains open.
why: It would improve the competitiveness of carbon-efficient acidic electrolysis.
key_works: D. Chen et al. (2025), *Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to ethylene in an acid-fed membrane electrode assembly at 10 A*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65831-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65831-8).

title: Low-energy carbonate recovery in CO₂ electrolysis
open: Minimize total energy for recovering CO₂ diverted into carbonate, including membrane water dissociation, acidification and gas separation, while increasing carbon utilization.
status: A persistent electrolyser problem. Acid-fed, bipolar and asymmetric membranes partly address carbon loss; the 2025 10 A demonstration still had limited single-pass ethylene carbon utilization.
why: It would make more captured or purchased CO₂ become product.
key_works: D. Chen et al. (2025), *Electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to ethylene in an acid-fed membrane electrode assembly at 10 A*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-65831-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-65831-8).

title: Salt- and flooding-resistant ethylene electrolysers over service lifetimes
open: Preserve gas access, ion transport and ethylene selectivity in stacks over long operation and repeated shutdowns, with infrequent maintenance.
status: Fang et al. reported over 1,000 hours at 200 mA cm⁻² with periodic membrane replacement and electrolyte refreshment, plus a five-cell stack, in work finalized in 2026. Whole-device service lifetime remains unresolved.
why: It addresses a major obstacle between laboratory cathodes and continuous production.
key_works: M. Fang et al. (2026), *Thousand-hour salt precipitation-free CO2-to-ethylene electrosynthesis at high current densities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z).

title: Predicting active copper after reconstruction
open: Predict working copper-site distributions and C₁/C₂ selectivity from initial structure, potential and gas history, including dissolution and redeposition.
status: A longstanding copper-electrocatalysis problem. A 2025 study observed nanocube reconstruction and copper-carbonyl migration, demonstrating the inadequacy of static starting-facet descriptions.
why: Synthesis could target the catalyst structure that persists in operation.
key_works: Y. Yang et al. (2025), *Operando probing dynamic migration of copper carbonyl during electrocatalytic CO2 reduction*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01359-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01359-w).

title: Selective third-carbon addition in CO electroreduction
open: Make C₂-to-C₃ coupling dominate competing ethylene, ethanol and hydrogen pathways while sustaining high rates and concentrated propanol output.
status: Selectivity beyond two carbons remains difficult. Strain-enhanced propanol electrosynthesis was demonstrated in 2026; practical selective C₃ production remains open.
why: It would extend renewable-carbon electrosynthesis to higher alcohols.
key_works: M. Wang et al. (2026), *Strain boosts propanol electrosynthesis from CO on copper*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01501-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01501-2).

title: Stable direct CO₂-to-methanol electrosynthesis
open: Combine durable methanol-selective molecular catalysis, low full-cell energy use and useful product concentration without catalyst loss or restructuring.
status: Song et al. reached 132 mA cm⁻² methanol partial current and 62% selectivity near pH 1 in 2025. Long-duration performance including recovery remains open.
why: It could supply a major liquid feedstock directly from CO₂ and electricity.
key_works: Y. Song et al. (2025), *Efficient CO2-to-methanol electrocatalysis in acidic media via microenvironment-tuned cobalt phthalocyanine*, [DOI:10.1038/s41565-025-02059-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-025-02059-z).

title: Multicarbon electrolysis of variable impure CO₂ feeds
open: Maintain controlled output as dilute CO₂ feeds vary in oxygen, sulfur and nitrogen impurities, with measured poisoning, regeneration and carbon balances.
status: Fang et al. tested dilute feeds and selected flue-gas impurities in 2026. Long-life operation under realistic mixed-impurity histories remains open.
why: It could reduce the upstream purification burden.
key_works: M. Fang et al. (2026), *Thousand-hour salt precipitation-free CO2-to-ethylene electrosynthesis at high current densities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67719-z).

title: Organic-crossover-resistant electrolyser anodes
open: Prevent crossover products from accelerating anode dissolution while retaining membrane conductivity and preserving the desired organic products.
status: Ka et al. showed in 2025 that aldehyde oxidation can destabilize iridium-oxide lattices. Durable mitigation across product mixtures remains unresolved.
why: It would preserve scarce catalysts and improve integrated product yield.
key_works: S. Ka et al. (2025), *Accelerated dissolution of iridium anode in the presence of organic compounds*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-63992-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-63992-0).

title: Practical iridium-free acidic oxygen evolution
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Demonstrate an acidic oxygen-evolution catalyst combining useful current density, low voltage and long membrane-electrode-assembly lifetime, with a complete dissolution balance.
status: Long sought. A 2025 cobalt study separated catalysis, corrosion and regeneration; self-reformation alone does not establish negligible material loss.
why: It could remove a critical-material bottleneck in PEM hydrogen production.
key_works: D. Simondson et al. (2025), *Decoupling the catalytic and degradation mechanisms of cobalt active sites during acidic water oxidation*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-025-01812-x).

title: The simultaneous DOE ultimate PEM electrolyser target
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Meet the official ultimate targets on one practical stack: 3 A cm⁻² at 1.6 V per cell, 0.125 mg cm⁻² total platinum-group metals and 80,000-hour lifetime, alongside cost requirements.
status: This is a combined target. A 2025 study achieved below 1.75 V at 4 A cm⁻² with 0.375 mg Ir cm⁻², advancing only some constraints.
why: It would reduce renewable hydrogen’s material and capital intensity.
key_works: U.S. DOE, *Technical Targets for Proton Exchange Membrane Electrolysis*, [official table, accessed 2026-10-06](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/technical-targets-proton-exchange-membrane-electrolysis); Y. Chen et al. (2025), *Support-free iridium hydroxide for high-efficiency proton-exchange membrane water electrolysis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-58019-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-58019-7).

title: Pure-water anion-exchange electrolysis with industrial durability
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Sustain high-current electrolysis with abundant-metal electrodes and pure-water feed while preserving membrane and ionomer conductivity through aging and interruptions.
status: A 2026 local-alkalinity design achieved 3 A cm⁻² at 2.08 V and approximately 1,400 hours at 1 A cm⁻². Simultaneous high-current efficiency and service-life durability remain open.
why: It would combine inexpensive catalysts with simpler liquid-feed handling.
key_works: J. Guo et al. (2026), *Local alkalinity enables high-performance pure water anion exchange membrane electrolysis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-69053-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69053-4).

title: Preventing iridium filaments across PEM electrolyser membranes
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Determine how dissolved iridium forms conducting cross-membrane paths and eliminate the resulting parasitic currents through materials and operating controls.
status: Heume et al. identified this degradation route in 2026 after 5,000 hours of industry-oriented operation; cells can continue functioning while losing efficiency.
why: It would eliminate hidden efficiency losses missed by simple operability tests.
key_works: C. Heume et al. (2026), *Cross-plane iridium-based filaments sap efficiency in proton exchange membrane electrolyzers*, [DOI:10.1016/j.joule.2025.102238](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.joule.2025.102238).

title: Durable cooperative oxygen evolution beyond single-site scaling
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Establish transferable low-overpotential oxygen evolution through cooperative sites, preserving the proposed mechanism and active inventory at practical currents.
status: Scaling-relation limits are longstanding. Kuai et al. showed in 2025 that dissolved iron participates in a cooperative solid–molecular NiFe mechanism; stable general implementation remains unresolved.
why: It could reduce losses beyond conventional single-site catalyst optimization.
key_works: C. Kuai et al. (2025), *Dissolved Fe species enable a cooperative solid–molecular mechanism for the oxygen evolution reaction on NiFe-based catalysts*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-025-01342-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-025-01342-5).

title: Efficient scalable photocatalytic water splitting with separated gases
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Combine efficient unconcentrated-sunlight use, separated hydrogen and oxygen streams and durable large-area operation with low mediator losses.
status: Pursued since the 1970s. A 2025 system achieved 2.47% solar-to-hydrogen efficiency and 1.21% outdoors in a 692.5 cm², week-long test.
why: It would provide direct solar fuel while simplifying gas separation.
key_works: H. Fu et al. (2025), *A scalable solar-driven photocatalytic system for separated H2 and O2 production from water*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56314-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56314-x).

title: Durable organic passivation of neutral-pH silicon photocathodes
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Preserve charge extraction and hydrogen evolution while preventing corrosion through defects, catalyst boundaries and aging in organic silicon-passivation layers.
status: Amze et al. reported six-hour stability for Pt-island/octadecyl-passivated silicon in work published online in 2025 and finalized in 2026. Long-life passivation remains open.
why: It could enable simple semiconductor protection in mild electrolytes.
key_works: M. Amze et al. (2026), *Hybrid island-and-sea approach for corrosion protection of Si photocathode in neutral-pH water splitting*, [DOI:10.1038/s41598-025-30589-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41598-025-30589-y).

title: Untreated-seawater electrolysis without chlorine or precipitation
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Operate complete electrolysers on variable natural seawater while suppressing chlorine chemistry, calcium/magnesium precipitation and corrosion with little conditioning.
status: A longstanding paired-electrode challenge. Separate 2026 advances include 1,500-hour simulated-seawater anode tests and natural-seawater cathode antifouling; the full integrated target remains open.
why: It would establish whether direct saline-water use offers a practical system advantage.
key_works: L.-l. Ma et al. (2026), *Breaking the activity-stability trade-off via dual-mechanism induced by rare earths for lasting seawater electrolysis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75978-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75978-7); Z. Li et al. (2026), *Cation-inhibitor and metal–support synergy for efficient and durable hydrogen evolution in natural seawater*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-72268-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72268-0).

title: Platinum-free fuel-cell cathodes with service-life stability
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Sustain high Fe–N–C cathode power under realistic air, humidity and load cycles while suppressing demetallation, corrosion and reactive-oxygen damage.
status: A decades-old target. A 2026 study reported strong accelerated-cycling durability, including H₂–air membrane-electrode assemblies; field service lifetime remains unresolved.
why: It would reduce platinum requirements while preserving fuel-cell power.
key_works: Y. Zeng et al. (2026), *Regulating in situ gaseous deposition to construct highly durable Fe–N–C oxygen-reduction fuel cell catalysts*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01482-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01482-2).

title: Retaining beneficial platinum strain without dissolution
subfield: Water splitting, hydrogen production and fuel cells
open: Preserve activity-enhancing platinum strain and accessible area through fuel-cell operation using resource-efficient supports.
status: A 2026 study identified a critical strain regime and demonstrated Pt-on-Ir films with under 10% loss after 30,000 cycles. Broad implementation with lower scarce-metal demand remains open.
why: It would preserve activity gains through useful device life.
key_works: Z. Zeng et al. (2026), *Critical surface strain regime for stable and active epitaxial platinum oxygen reduction electrocatalysts*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-026-02108-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-026-02108-4).

title: Unified chemical–mechanical prediction of lithium dendrite penetration
open: Predict where and when lithium penetrates solid electrolytes using coupled decomposition, stress, microstructure and transport, with validation across materials.
status: A longstanding battery problem. Fincher et al. showed in 2026 that dendrites can propagate at stresses up to 75% below mechanical-fracture expectations because corrosion accompanies growth.
why: It would make dendrite avoidance a predictive design task.
key_works: C. D. Fincher et al. (2026), *Electrochemical corrosion accompanies dendrite growth in solid electrolytes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10279-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10279-z).

title: Void-free lithium stripping at useful areal capacity
open: Maintain electrolyte contact during deep lithium stripping at practical current, capacity and low pressure while also avoiding plating-induced shorts.
status: Contact loss is longstanding. An August 2026 study linked void suppression to current multiplied by stripping capacity and improved alloy behavior; simultaneous void and dendrite control remains open.
why: It would permit full lithium utilization with lighter pressure hardware.
key_works: X. Ji et al. (2026), *Void suppressive lithium anodes for all-solid-state batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02729-w).

title: Stable high-voltage sulfide-solid-electrolyte interfaces
open: Prevent continuing sulfide oxidation and reduction at both electrodes while preserving low-resistance ion transport and mechanical contact during high-voltage cycling.
status: Known since sulfide electrolytes became prominent. A 2025 electrophile-reduction strategy suppressed decomposition and dendrites; lifetime and manufacturing tolerance remain unresolved.
why: It would translate high ionic conductivity into durable high-energy cells.
key_works: W. Zhang et al. (2025), *Revitalizing interphase in all-solid-state Li metal batteries by electrophile reduction*, [DOI:10.1038/s41563-024-02064-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-024-02064-y).

title: Long-life 500 Wh/kg-class anode-free cells
open: Retain anode-free cell energy above 500 Wh/kg while extending deep-cycle and calendar life with lean electrolyte, finite lithium inventory and manufacturable pressure requirements.
status: Liu et al. demonstrated 508 Wh/kg, 2.7 Ah cells in 2026: 100 full-depth cycles or 250 cycles at 80% depth, both to 80% capacity retention.
why: It would preserve anode-free energy-density gains through useful product life.
key_works: L. Liu et al. (2026), *Planar Li deposition and dissolution enable practical anode-free pouch cells*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10402-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10402-0).

title: Fast charging combined with slow discharge in lithium-metal cells
open: Sustain lithium reversibility under fast charging followed by slow discharge in high-loading, lean-electrolyte cells, including cold operation and calendar exposure.
status: Many laboratory gains used the opposite protocol. Kim et al. addressed this degradation mode with an electrolyte diluent in 2026; broad practical operating envelopes remain open.
why: It would align lithium-metal chemistry with vehicle and mobile-device use.
key_works: M. Kim et al. (2026), *Electrolyte diluent with large electrostatic potential difference for fast charging and slow discharging lithium metal batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-69870-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69870-7).

title: Practical lean-electrolyte lithium–sulfur lifetime
open: Combine low electrolyte-to-sulfur ratio, high sulfur loading and limited lithium excess with long full-cell life, including packaging in energy-density accounting.
status: A decades-old commercialization barrier. A 2025 study reported 493 Wh/kg excluding external packaging at 2.4 μL electrolyte/mg sulfur, with 70% retention after 220 cycles.
why: It would convert sulfur’s inexpensive capacity into durable lightweight storage.
key_works: H. Cho et al. (2025), *Interconvertible and rejuvenated Lewis acidic electrolyte additive for lean electrolyte lithium sulfur batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-62169-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-62169-z).

title: Predictive Li₂S deposition in concentrated polysulfide electrolytes
open: Predict deposition location, morphology and reversibility from concentration and operating history, including competing surface and solution pathways under lean conditions.
status: Long unresolved. Zhou et al. directly imaged concentration-driven interfacial segregation in 2026 and connected it with competing Li₂S deposition routes.
why: It would guide electrodes that avoid premature passivation and inaccessible sulfur.
key_works: S. Zhou et al. (2026), *Revealing competitive interfacial reactions in high-energy Li–S batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09473-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09473-2).

title: Suppressing parasitic oxygen chemistry in rechargeable Li–O₂ cells
open: Cycle oxygen reduction and evolution with complete oxygen and charge balances while preventing singlet-oxygen damage to electrolyte, carbon and binder.
status: Rechargeability has been problematic since early nonaqueous Li–O₂ research. A 2025 study established Marcus-kinetic control of singlet/triplet oxygen production from superoxide, providing a possible intervention.
why: It would improve access to the chemistry’s high theoretical specific energy.
key_works: S. Mondal et al. (2025), *Marcus kinetics control singlet and triplet oxygen evolving from superoxide*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09587-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09587-7).

title: Reversible magnesium–sulfur conversion with practical loading
open: Sustain reversible MgS formation and oxidation at high sulfur loading and low electrolyte content, with limited magnesium trapping and anode consumption.
status: A persistent multivalent-conversion problem. A 2026 solvation strategy yielded 120 laboratory cycles and an initial pouch-cell demonstration.
why: It could combine abundant constituents with high storage capacity.
key_works: J. Li et al. (2026), *Solvating magnesium polysulfides enables low–barrier speciation for magnesium sulfur batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-70598-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70598-7).

title: Long-lived room-temperature calcium-metal full cells
open: Combine reversible calcium plating with useful high-voltage positive electrodes, preserving electrolyte compatibility and calcium inventory through room-temperature cycling.
status: Calcium reversibility remains an active barrier. A 2026 organoborate-solvation study made progress, while a broadly durable anode–electrolyte–cathode combination remains unavailable.
why: It would diversify storage beyond lithium and monovalent chemistry.
key_works: S. Li et al. (2026), *Strongly-coordinating organoborates with eccentric solvation structure enable secondary calcium metal battery*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-73484-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73484-4).

title: Zinc-metal reversibility without excess zinc or electrolyte
open: Sustain aqueous cells with thin zinc and lean electrolyte while controlling hydrogen evolution, corrosion and morphology during cycling and idle periods.
status: A longstanding problem. A 2026 low-surface-tension electrolyte controlled zinc nucleation; shelf life and finite-inventory cycling remain joint constraints.
why: It would improve the complete-system lifetime of inexpensive zinc storage.
key_works: H. Wang et al. (2026), *Regulating zinc nucleation and growth with low-surface-tension electrolytes for practical aqueous zinc metal batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-68393-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-68393-5).

title: Wide-voltage aqueous batteries without concentrated-salt penalties
open: Sustain high-voltage aqueous full cells with good conductivity and low electrolyte cost, measuring water decomposition directly.
status: Water-in-salt approaches expanded apparent windows in the 2010s. A 2026 study demonstrated hydrophobic interphases in 3-molal zinc electrolyte; transferable low-cost full-cell stability remains open.
why: It would combine aqueous safety with higher usable energy density.
key_works: G. Li et al. (2026), *Hydrophobic liquid electrolyte interphases for efficient aqueous zinc batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41565-026-02187-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41565-026-02187-0).

title: Hard-carbon sodium storage with low irreversible inventory loss
open: Control desolvation and interphase formation so hard carbon simultaneously retains sodium inventory, rate capability and lifetime across precursor batches.
status: Studied since around 2000. A 2026 MOF-glass coating improved transport and interphase stability; precursor-independent control remains unresolved.
why: It would improve sodium-ion energy utilization and manufacturing consistency.
key_works: J. Zhao et al. (2026), *Metal–organic framework glass enables durable sodium-ion storage for hard carbon negative electrodes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-75060-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-75060-2).

title: Manufacturing-tolerant high-nickel cathode chemomechanics
open: Prevent oxygen loss, pore evolution and mechanical damage while retaining energy density across realistic loading, voltage, temperature and manufacturing variation.
status: A longstanding tradeoff. A 2026 uniform-pore architecture showed negligible degradation under studied conditions; robustness to industrial heterogeneity remains open.
why: It would retain high capacity without continually increasing inactive protective material.
key_works: D. Eum et al. (2026), *Uniform pore structure enables negligible degradation in undoped and uncoated Ni-rich cathodes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-026-01988-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-026-01988-w).

title: Reversible oxygen redox without interfacial destruction
open: Repeatedly use oxygen-redox capacity in lithium-rich manganese oxides without voltage decay, oxygen escape or oxidation of adjacent sulfide electrolyte.
status: Irreversibility has persisted for decades. A 2026 study investigated and mitigated coupled lattice-oxygen and interface changes; simultaneous retention of voltage, capacity and interfaces remains open.
why: It would increase capacity beyond transition-metal redox while controlling degradation.
key_works: Y. Wu et al. (2026), *Interplay between oxygen redox and interfacial stability of Li-rich positive electrodes in sulfide-based all-solid-state batteries*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-74601-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-74601-z).

title: Transferable electrolyte design rules for preventing cell thermal runaway
open: Predict and prevent full-cell runaway from charged-electrode–electrolyte reactions, including gas generation, aging and internal contact changes.
status: A longstanding safety gap. A 2026 thermally polymerizing electrolyte enabled runaway-free ampere-hour sodium-ion cells under tested conditions; transfer across chemistries and abuse modes remains open.
why: It would make chemical safety improvements predictable across cell designs.
key_works: J. Zhang et al. (2026), *Thermal runaway-free ampere-hour-level Na-ion battery via polymerizable non-flammable electrolyte*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-026-02032-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-026-02032-7).

title: Predicting reversible versus destructive water attack on MOFs
open: Predict when water-induced coordination changes are reversible and when they produce permanent framework damage, including defects, cycling and mixed guests.
status: Stability has been central since MOFs emerged. A 2026 study showed reversible water-stabilized dangling carboxylates even in water-stable UiO-66.
why: It would enable dependable porous materials under wet operating conditions.
key_works: Y. Fu et al. (2026), *Water-generated dangling linkers in a metal-organic framework*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-70247-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-70247-z).

title: Material-based hydrogen storage meeting complete system targets
open: Meet DOE ultimate usable system capacities of 6.5 wt% hydrogen and 50 g/L simultaneously with delivery, refueling, cost and lifetime requirements.
status: A decades-old target. Screening nearly half a million MOFs produced high-performing materials in 2019; complete systems must also account for vessels, cooling and unusable residual hydrogen.
why: It would support compact hydrogen transport with competitive system mass and volume.
key_works: U.S. DOE, *DOE Technical Targets for Onboard Hydrogen Storage for Light-Duty Vehicles*, [official table, accessed 2026-10-06](https://www.energy.gov/cmei/fuels/doe-technical-targets-onboard-hydrogen-storage-light-duty-vehicles); A. Ahmed et al. (2019), *Exceptional hydrogen storage achieved by screening nearly half a million metal-organic frameworks*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-019-09365-w).

title: Predicting zeolitic imidazolate framework topology from synthesis conditions
open: Predict the ZIF topology obtained from specified metal, linker, solvent and protocol, including competition with dense phases.
status: Reticular synthesis remains partly empirical. An automated iterative strategy published online in 2025 and in a 2026 issue doubled discovery rate over random exploration; transferable topology selection remains open.
why: It would make targeted pore networks accessible with fewer experiments.
key_works: Z. Rong et al. (2026), *Algorithmic iterative reticular synthesis of zeolitic imidazolate framework crystals*, [DOI:10.1038/s44160-025-00939-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44160-025-00939-9).

title: Macroscopic ordered two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks
open: Grow processable macroscopic or large-area 2D COF crystals with controlled stacking, accessible porosity and preserved order after activation and cycling.
status: A challenge since the 2000s. Three single-crystal 2D COF isomers were resolved by electron diffraction in 2026; scalable ordered material remains a further target.
why: It would connect designed molecular pores to practical adsorption and electronic applications.
key_works: B. Yu et al. (2026), *Single-crystal 2D covalent organic frameworks for high-capacity methane storage*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-69614-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-69614-7).

title: Suppressing illumination-driven mixed-halide segregation over lifetime
open: Preserve homogeneous wide-bandgap mixed-halide compositions under light, bias and thermal cycling while retaining transport and additive stability.
status: Recognized since the mid-2010s. Zhu et al. reported suppressed segregation on 1 October 2026; broad composition coverage and complete operational lifetime remain unresolved.
why: It would preserve the bandgap and voltage required for tandem photovoltaics.
key_works: X. Zhu et al. (2026), *Wide-bandgap perovskite with homogeneous crystallization and suppressed halogen segregation for efficient perovskite-organic tandem solar cells*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-78267-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-78267-5).

title: Chemically robust perovskite tandems under reverse bias
open: Prevent irreversible perovskite and interface chemistry during repeated partial-shading reverse-bias events while maintaining efficiency and manufacturability.
status: A modern tandem-deployment problem. Graded dielectric layers improved resistance in 2026; robustness across defects and outdoor stress histories remains open.
why: It would prevent permanent damage from ordinary shading and current mismatch.
key_works: L. Wang et al. (2026), *Improving the stability of monolithic perovskite/silicon tandems against reverse-bias stress using graded dielectric layers*, [DOI:10.1038/s41560-026-02067-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41560-026-02067-w).

title: Oxidation-stable lead-free tin-halide semiconductor interfaces
open: Maintain the required tin oxidation state and suppress uncontrolled self-doping at surfaces and grain boundaries during sustained device operation.
status: A persistent lead-free-perovskite barrier. Volatile-coordination surface reconstruction improved tin-halide transistor stability in 2026; transferable long-life redox control remains open.
why: It would support less-lead-dependent optoelectronics with stable performance.
key_works: G. Park et al. (2026), *Tin perovskite transistors stabilized through volatile coordination*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-026-10714-1](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10714-1).

title: Predicting inorganic synthesis products from transport kinetics
subfield: Inorganic solid-state synthesis and corrosion chemistry
open: Predict intermediates, phase fractions and final products of multicomponent powder reactions from precursor and thermal history, including correlated diffusion and metastability.
status: A longstanding gap between phase thermodynamics and synthesis. A 2026 Ba–Ti–O study incorporated correlated transport; transfer across chemical systems remains open.
why: It would reduce failed attempts to synthesize predicted functional materials.
key_works: V. Karan et al. (2026), *Ion correlations explain kinetic selectivity in diffusion-limited solid-state synthesis reactions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41563-026-02596-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02596-5).
