title: Predicting chloride-pit initiation from real surface microstructure
subfield: Inorganic solid-state synthesis and corrosion chemistry
open: Predict distributions of pit-initiation potentials and times from inclusions, passive-film chemistry and processing history, enabling resistance under variable chloride exposure.
status: Studied for over a century. A 2026 study resolved how grinding and MnS inclusions affect stainless-steel pitting; a transferable initiation law remains absent.
why: It would connect surface processing to reliable infrastructure lifetime.
key_works: S. Wang, M. Nishimoto and I. Muto (2026), *Grinding-induced degradation in the pitting corrosion resistance of stainless steel: insights into passive film and MnS*, [DOI:10.1038/s41529-026-00750-7](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41529-026-00750-7).

title: Predictive high-temperature hydrogen embrittlement chemistry
subfield: Inorganic solid-state synthesis and corrosion chemistry
open: Predict damage when hydrogen trapping, carbide decomposition, methane formation and deformation interact across alloy compositions and thermal histories.
status: Hydrogen embrittlement is a century-old problem. A 2026 study identified vacancy-mediated carbide reactions and localized methane in nickel superalloys; transferable high-temperature prediction remains open.
why: It would support materials and operating limits for hydrogen-containing high-temperature fuels.
key_works: S. Kong et al. (2026), *Hydrogen-induced damage in Ni-based superalloys at elevated temperatures*, [DOI:10.1038/s41563-026-02680-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41563-026-02680-w).

title: Substrate-oxygen assignment in photosystem II
open: Determine experimentally which two oxygen atoms form O₂, distinguishing O5–O6 coupling from the competing O3–O6 proposal.
status: A 2026 calculation proposed O3–O6 coupling, while new structural measurements located the additional S₃-state oxygen without directly identifying the reacting pair. The remaining target is an experimentally discriminating atom assignment.

title: Absolute methanol desorption yield per hydrogen-abstraction cycle
open: Directly count intact methanol molecules ejected from water-rich and CO-rich ice during hydrogen-abstraction–addition cycles, separating desorption from conversion into other surface products.
status: Gadallah and colleagues’ 2026 experiments measured methanol depletion, but hydrogen background prevented direct gas-phase detection. The reported \(12\pm3\%\) depletion on amorphous water ice is an upper bound on cumulative desorption, not a measured probability per reaction.

title: Methanol deuteration inherited through star formation
open: Explain, with one isotope-resolved reaction network, why the CH₂DOH/CH₃OD ratio differs between low-mass and high-mass protostars, and determine how much reflects cold-ice formation versus later hydrogen–deuterium exchange.
status: The first secure prestellar CH₃OD detection, reported in 2025 for L1448, gives a ratio of 2.8–8.5 under the authors’ excitation assumptions. That supplies a missing starting-point measurement, while leaving the evolutionary changes to be explained.

title: Delayed chromium(VI) rebound after reductive remediation
open: Predict and prevent renewed Cr(VI) formation as chromium–iron hydroxides age and manganese changes oxidation state, including repeated changes in oxygen exposure and pH.
status: Experiments published in 2025 found substantially greater Cr(VI) release after mineral transformation under the tested conditions. The remaining target is durable control across the changing chemistry of treated residues.

title: Uniform maximum atomic excess charge
open: Prove that a nucleus of charge \(Z\) can bind at most \(Z+C\) electrons, with \(C\) independent of \(Z\), for the full nonrelativistic many-electron Coulomb Hamiltonian.
status: The Hartree–Fock analogue is established, while the interacting Schrödinger problem remains open. A 2025 result gives the explicit bound \(N_c<1.1185Z+4Z^{1/3}\) for \(Z\ge4\), which still permits an excess increasing with nuclear charge.

title: Proton-and-electron-only recycling of triphenylphosphine oxide
open: Reduce ordinary triphenylphosphine oxide to triphenylphosphine using electricity and a proton source, without stoichiometric silanes, hydrides, or halogenating activators.
status: A 2026 study achieved 90% yield for a specially designed fused dipyridyl phosphine oxide; extending this proton-coupled reduction to commodity phosphine oxides remains open.
why: Could close phosphorus-reagent cycles in widely used organic reactions.
key_works: A. Laverny et al. (2026), *Proton-coupled electrochemical reduction of a phosphine oxide*, [DOI:10.1016/j.chempr.2026.102946](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chempr.2026.102946).

title: Automated α(2,3)-sialylation of C4-substituted galactose acceptors
open: Install an α(2,3)-sialic-acid linkage on a galactose acceptor whose C4 oxygen must remain substituted, with reliable coupling during automated solid-phase assembly.
status: Automated synthesis of nine sialylated human-milk oligosaccharides was demonstrated in 2026. The C4-substituted model acceptor gave only traces of the desired product; exposing both C3 and C4 hydroxyls improved isolated yield to 35%.
why: Removes a specific structural restriction from automated glycan synthesis.
key_works: Y.-T. Kuo, K. L. M. Hoang and P. H. Seeberger (2026), *Synthesis of sialylated human milk oligosaccharides by automated glycan assembly*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-73028-w](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73028-w).

title: All-weight extension of atomic ionization bounds
open: Prove \(N_c(Z)<b(s)Z+c(s)Z^{1/3}\) for every \(s\ge1\), where \(b(s)=\max_{0\le t\le1}(1+t^{s-1})/(1+t^s)\) and \(c(s)\) is finite. The unresolved range is \(s>3\), including quantitative control of \(c(s)\).
status: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz proved the weighted estimate for \(1<s\le3\) and explicitly conjectured its extension in 2025.
why: Since \(b(s)\to1\), the extension could substantially strengthen finite-atom ionization bounds.
key_works: Hundertmark, Pattakos and Schulz (2025), *On the Excess Charge Problem of Atoms*, Remark 2.3, [arXiv:2504.18487](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.18487).

title: Uniform first-ionization-energy bound
open: Prove that \(E_Z(Z-1)-E_Z(Z)\le C\) for neutral atoms, uniformly in nuclear charge, with the complete electron–electron interaction.
status: A longstanding component of the ionization conjecture. Solovej proved the Hartree–Fock version; the full Schrödinger problem remains open because available total-energy asymptotics do not control the required order-one difference.
why: Places the bounded energy scale of outer-electron chemistry on a many-body foundation.
key_works: J. P. Solovej (2003), *The Ionization Conjecture in Hartree-Fock Theory*, [arXiv:math-ph/0012026](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0012026); M. Lewin (2025), *Some open mathematical problems concerning charged quantum particles*, [DOI:10.5802/crphys.249](https://doi.org/10.5802/crphys.249).

title: Uniform outer-electron radius bound
open: Define \(R_m(Z)\) so that a fixed number \(m>0\) of electrons lie outside that radius in a neutral atom. Establish \(Z\)-independent bounds, with the appropriate dependence on \(m\), for the full interacting theory.
status: Corresponding Hartree–Fock ionization-radius results are proved. Comparable exact many-electron density-tail control remains a decades-old problem.
why: Explains why chemically relevant valence length scales need not shrink with the atomic core.
key_works: J. P. Solovej (2003), *The Ionization Conjecture in Hartree-Fock Theory*, [arXiv:math-ph/0012026](https://arxiv.org/abs/math-ph/0012026).

title: Chemical periodicity from the correlated atomic Hamiltonian
open: Derive a precise large-\(Z\) recurrence law for valence observables or low-energy spectra of interacting atoms, with controlled corrections. The law must accommodate actual shell-order exceptions.
status: Bjerg and Solovej proved periodicity for a Thomas–Fermi mean-field operator in 2025. Extending such a result to the correlated many-electron Hamiltonian remains open.
why: Derives recurring chemical scales from quantum mechanics with an explicit range of validity.
key_works: A. Bjerg and J. P. Solovej (2025), *Periodicity of Atomic Structure in a Thomas-Fermi Mean-Field Model*, [DOI:10.1007/s00220-025-05418-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-025-05418-y).

title: Sharp three-dimensional Lieb–Thirring kinetic constant
open: Determine the optimal three-dimensional fermionic kinetic-energy constant, equivalently the sharp Lieb–Thirring spectral constant at \(\gamma=1\). Resolve whether the semiclassical value is optimal.
status: Open since the 1970s. The semiclassical constant was proved for shifted Coulomb Hamiltonians in 2025; arbitrary admissible potentials remain unresolved.
why: Sharpens electronic kinetic-energy lower bounds and quantitative stability estimates for matter.
key_works: T. C. Corso and T. Ried (2025), *On a Variational Problem Related to the Cwikel–Lieb–Rozenblum and Lieb–Thirring Inequalities*, [DOI:10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00220-024-05216-y); Corso, T. Weidl and Z. Zeng (2025), *Lieb–Thirring inequalities for the shifted Coulomb Hamiltonian*, [DOI:10.4171/JST/574](https://doi.org/10.4171/JST/574).

title: Three-dimensional noninteracting ground-state representability
open: Characterize which interacting ground-state densities in three dimensions are reproducible by a noninteracting ground state in a local scalar potential, including ensemble requirements and potential regularity.
status: Longstanding. Corso proved a rigorous one-dimensional spinless representability and Kohn–Sham existence theory in March 2026; the corresponding three-dimensional characterization remains open.
why: Establishes when an exact Kohn–Sham reference system exists.
key_works: T. C. Corso (2026), *A rigorous formulation of density functional theory for spinless fermions in one dimension*, [DOI:10.1007/s11005-026-02051-1](https://doi.org/10.1007/s11005-026-02051-1).

title: Stable inversion from a three-dimensional density to its potential
open: Establish quantitative stability estimates for reconstructing external or Kohn–Sham potentials from perturbed three-dimensional densities, including explicit assumptions near degeneracies.
status: Corso and Laestadius obtained quantitative Hohenberg–Kohn results with Lipschitz control in one dimension in 2025. General three-dimensional error amplification remains inadequately characterized.
why: Makes density inversion and learned inverse functionals numerically accountable.
key_works: T. C. Corso and A. Laestadius (2025), *A quantitative Hohenberg-Kohn theorem and the unexpected regularity of density functional theory in one spatial dimension*, [arXiv:2512.04726](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04726).

title: Hohenberg–Kohn mapping for the physical total current
open: Determine whether particle density and physical total current uniquely determine scalar and vector potentials, modulo gauge, under precise ground-state assumptions. Alternatively, construct a counterexample identifying the missing information.
status: Standard paramagnetic-current uniqueness fails, and proposed total-current arguments have known defects. The physical-current mapping remains unresolved after the 2021 analysis of Diener’s construction.
why: Supports reliable density-functional descriptions of magnetic response and molecular currents.
key_works: A. Laestadius, M. Penz and E. I. Tellgren (2021), *Revisiting density-functional theory of the total current density*, [DOI:10.1088/1361-648X/abf784](https://doi.org/10.1088/1361-648X/abf784).

title: Generic coupled-cluster singles-and-doubles root counts
open: Derive a usable formula for the generic number of isolated complex CCSD amplitude solutions as electron and orbital counts vary, distinguishing arbitrary algebraic systems from physical two-body Hamiltonians.
status: Algebraic geometry provides bounds and special cases. The Grassmannian CCS degree is solved; arbitrary-size CCSD root counts are not.
why: Quantifies solution multiplicity and the completeness requirements of continuation algorithms.
key_works: F. M. Faulstich, B. Sturmfels and S. Sverrisdóttir (2025), *Algebraic Varieties in Quantum Chemistry*, [DOI:10.1007/s10208-024-09657-8](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10208-024-09657-8).

title: Computable coupled-cluster truncation error certificates
open: Produce rigorous, evaluable error bars for practical truncated coupled-cluster energies, with tests detecting failure of the assumptions behind the certificate.
status: Recent analysis proves local well-posedness and a posteriori estimates under structural assumptions. Inexpensively evaluating stability constants and missing-correlation bounds for difficult molecules remains open.
why: Distinguishes convergence of the amplitude solver from chemical accuracy.
key_works: M. Hassan, Y. Maday and Y. Wang (2023), *Analysis of the Single Reference Coupled Cluster Method for Electronic Structure Calculations: The Discrete Coupled Cluster Equations*, [arXiv:2311.00637](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.00637).

title: Guaranteed numerical errors for nonconvex Kohn–Sham calculations
open: Give computable energy-error bounds for nonconvex Kohn–Sham functionals, accounting for discretization and self-consistency while distinguishing local stationary states from the global minimum.
status: Guaranteed bounds were obtained for periodic equations with convex density functionals in 2025. Many practical exchange-correlation approximations violate that central hypothesis.
why: Makes numerical phase orderings and energy differences testable independently of functional approximation error.
key_works: A. Bordignon et al. (2025), *Fully Guaranteed and Computable Error Bounds on the Energy for Periodic Kohn–Sham Equations with Convex Density Functionals*, [DOI:10.1137/25M1735676](https://doi.org/10.1137/25M1735676).

title: Certified atom-centered basis errors for correlated reaction energies
open: Bound finite atom-centered-basis errors in correlated reaction energies with computable constants, including error cancellation between reactants and products.
status: Dupuy, Dusson and Lygatsika established a posteriori estimates for linear Schrödinger operators in atomic-orbital bases in 2025. General correlated many-electron reaction-energy certificates remain beyond that result.
why: Separates basis incompleteness from correlation errors in reference thermochemistry.
key_works: M.-S. Dupuy, G. Dusson and I.-M. Lygatsika (2025), *A Posteriori Error Estimates for Schrödinger Operators Discretized with Linear Combinations of Atomic Orbitals*, [DOI:10.1137/24M1700697](https://doi.org/10.1137/24M1700697).

title: Density-matrix embedding convergence beyond weak coupling
open: Establish convergence of density-matrix embedding toward strongly correlated states as fragments enlarge, with computable observable errors and criteria identifying spurious self-consistent branches.
status: A 2025 analysis proved existence, conditional uniqueness and first-order exactness near the noninteracting limit. Strong-coupling convergence and fragment-size error bars remain unresolved.
why: Enables trustworthy calculations for catalysts and correlated solids beyond isolated active spaces.
key_works: E. Cancès et al. (2025), *Analysis of density matrix embedding theory around the non-interacting limit*, [DOI:10.1002/cpa.22244](https://doi.org/10.1002/cpa.22244).

title: Smooth adaptive active spaces through changing chemical bonding
open: Change the correlated orbital space automatically during bond breaking, charge transfer and spin crossings while preserving smooth energies and forces and controlling discarded correlation.
status: The 2025 weighted active-space protocol reduces discontinuities and supports multireference learned potentials. A reliable general criterion for admitting newly essential orbitals remains open.
why: Enables multireference dynamics without repeated manual orbital selection.
key_works: A. Seal et al. (2025), *Weighted active space protocol for multireference machine-learned potentials*, [DOI:10.1073/pnas.2513693122](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2513693122).

title: Controlled omission of induced many-body downfolding terms
open: Bound errors caused by discarding induced three- and higher-body operators from effective electronic Hamiltonians, and select necessary terms without restoring the original computational cost.
status: Coupled-cluster downfolding has compressed large orbital spaces for quantum simulations. General inexpensive control of operator-rank truncation remains missing despite successful examples.
why: Determines whether small quantum calculations faithfully represent larger chemical systems.
key_works: N. P. Bauman et al. (2026), *Coupled cluster downfolding theory in simulations of correlated systems on quantum hardware*, [DOI:10.1103/b1t6-ln6v](https://doi.org/10.1103/b1t6-ln6v); [arXiv:2507.01199](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.01199).

title: Scalable certificates of ensemble two-particle representability
open: Identify chemically useful classes where a two-electron reduced density matrix can be certified as ensemble-representable, or excluded, with practical resources and explicit tolerances.
status: The unrestricted problem is computationally hard. Oña et al. demonstrated purification-based tests on two-, three- and four-electron examples in 2025–2026; scalable certified subclasses remain open.
why: Prevents unphysical reduced densities from contaminating energies and reconstructed quantum measurements.
key_works: O. B. Oña et al. (2026), *Determining the Ensemble N-Representability of Reduced Density Matrices*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01788](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01788).

title: Joint representability of a manifold of transition densities
open: Certify that approximate state densities and transition reduced density matrices arise from one common orthonormal set of many-electron states, including reconstruction from noisy measurements.
status: A 2025 transition-density representability construction supplied small-system tests. Scalable joint consistency across an entire spectroscopic manifold remains a further target.
why: Enforces compatible transition moments, oscillator strengths and nonlinear responses.
key_works: G. E. Massaccesi et al. (2025), *Determining the N-representability of transition reduced density matrices*, [DOI:10.1063/5.0275683](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0275683).

title: Selecting the physical branch of self-consistent Green’s functions
open: Establish criteria selecting the physical equilibrium solution among self-consistent GF2 or GW branches, while distinguishing genuine metastability from diagrammatic-truncation artifacts.
status: Multiple solutions are documented. Pokhilko and Zgid’s 2025 homotopy method tracks Dyson-equation branches, including NdNiO₂ examples, without resolving universal physical branch selection.
why: Prevents a converged numerical solution from receiving an unjustified thermodynamic interpretation.
key_works: P. Pokhilko and D. Zgid (2025), *Homotopy continuation method for solving Dyson equation fully self-consistently: Theory and application to NdNiO2*, [DOI:10.1063/5.0288359](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0288359).

title: Practical dynamics through coupled-cluster ground-state intersections
open: Implement analytic gradients and nonadiabatic couplings for CVX-SCC, then demonstrate stable dynamics and correct population transfer through ground/excited-state conical intersections.
status: Stoll, Rossi and Koch’s September 2026 preprint reports correct static intersection topology in several molecules. Gradients, coupling vectors and dynamics remain future developments.
why: Connects coupled-cluster accuracy to photochemical yields at ground-state funnels.
key_works: L. Stoll, F. Rossi and H. Koch (2026), *Resolving the ground state intersection problem in coupled cluster theory*, [arXiv:2609.10164](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10164).

title: Error bars for very narrow molecular resonance widths
open: Compute molecular resonance widths with uncertainties substantially smaller than the widths themselves, including correlation, basis and complex-variable approximation errors.
status: Complex-variable EOM-CCSD is established. A 2025 resolution-of-the-identity implementation documents qualitatively unreliable widths when approximation errors approach exceptionally narrow resonances.
why: Determines whether temporary molecular ions survive long enough to undergo attachment chemistry.
key_works: S. Camps, C. Utku, J. Creutzberg and T.-C. Jagau (2025), *Complex-Variable Equation-of-Motion Coupled-Cluster Singles and Doubles Theory with the Resolution-of-the-Identity Approximation*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpca.5c01313](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.5c01313).

title: Dissociative attachment on coupled complex potential-energy surfaces
open: Predict absolute electron-attachment cross sections and fragment branching using coupled complex surfaces, autodetachment and quantum nuclear motion, connecting incident continua to resolved product channels.
status: Mondal and Bravaya extended projected-CAP gradients and couplings to multireference approaches in 2025. Broadly validated polyatomic scattering dynamics using these surfaces remains open.
why: Explains low-energy electron chemistry in radiation damage, plasmas and interstellar environments.
key_works: S. Mondal and K. B. Bravaya (2025), *Analytic Nuclear Gradients for Complex Potential Energy Surfaces: A Projected CAP Approach*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c00418](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c00418).

title: Molecular Auger branching beyond local decay approximations
open: Calculate absolute channel-resolved Auger widths with multicenter continuum emission and correlated final states, identifying when local decay approximations alter branching.
status: Fouda et al. benchmarked multiconfiguration pair-density-functional spectra for 20 organic molecules in 2025 using a one-center decay approximation. Scalable nonlocal continuum treatment remains a bottleneck.
why: Makes core-hole spectroscopy quantitatively informative about electron correlation and radiation chemistry.
key_works: A. E. Fouda et al. (2025), *Computation of Auger Electron Spectra in Organic Molecules with Multiconfiguration Pair-Density Functional Theory*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpca.5c01789](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpca.5c01789).

title: Quantitative core-level shakeup intensities in strongly correlated molecules
open: Predict shakeup-satellite energies and absolute relative intensities when multiple valence excitations and strong correlation contribute, with controlled improvements beyond standard GW-plus-cumulant theory.
status: A 2025 implementation reproduced dominant satellite energies within approximately 0.5 eV for tested molecules containing up to 40 atoms. Comparable intensity accuracy across strongly correlated systems remains unestablished.
why: Makes weak photoelectron features useful for identifying charge redistribution.
key_works: J. Kockläuner and D. Golze (2025), *GW Plus Cumulant Approach for Predicting Core-Level Shakeup Satellites in Large Molecules*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01754](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.4c01754).

title: Hydrogen-molecule QED at the newest experimental resolution
open: Calculate higher-order radiative, recoil and nonadiabatic terms needed to place theoretical uncertainties below the best H₂ interval measurements, with correlated uncertainty budgets across isotopologues.
status: Recent theory resolved earlier discrepancies. Pachucki and Komasa reported sub-MHz progress in 2025; Doran et al. reported a 175-kHz dissociation-energy determination in 2026.
why: Strengthens molecular tests of QED and searches for additional interactions.
key_works: K. Pachucki and J. Komasa (2025), *From First-Principles to Quantum Electrodynamics: Pushing the Limits of Theory with the Hydrogen Molecule*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01702](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jctc.5c01702); I. Doran et al. (2026), *Ionization and dissociation energies of molecular hydrogen*, [DOI:10.1103/42c4-pc1s](https://doi.org/10.1103/42c4-pc1s).

title: Independently determining nuclear masses and radii from molecular spectra
open: Measure sufficiently independent transitions across H₂⁺, HD⁺ and related isotopologues to disentangle nuclear mass ratios, radii and shared theoretical corrections without assuming the desired constants.
status: Precision H₂⁺ spectroscopy yielded a proton–electron mass-ratio determination in 2025. Independent joint extraction of the broader constant set needs additional sensitivities and controlled theory correlations.
why: Cross-checks atomic spectroscopy, mass measurements and nuclear-size determinations.
key_works: S. Alighanbari, M. R. Schenkel, V. I. Korobov and S. Schiller (2025), *High-accuracy laser spectroscopy of H2+ and the proton–electron mass ratio*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09306-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09306-2).

title: Quantitative microscopic prediction of chiral spin selectivity
open: Predict spin-polarization magnitude, sign and temperature dependence from molecular structure and contacts without fitting artificially large spin–orbit coupling.
status: Competing mechanisms reproduce subsets of CISS experiments. A 2025 ab initio Hubbard-model parametrization demonstrates consequential electron–vibration effects, but a transferable quantitative theory remains unresolved.
why: Enables rational design of chiral spin filters and spin-dependent reactions.
key_works: D. K. A. Phan Huu et al. (2025), *Ab initio parametrization of a generalized Hubbard model in a molecule displaying chirality-induced spin selectivity*, [DOI:10.1038/s43246-025-00821-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43246-025-00821-3).

title: Separating molecular and contact contributions to CISS
open: Measure intrinsic molecular spin filtering and electrode-interface selectivity independently in the same device, with controls for current direction, magnetization, handedness and nonlinear voltage response.
status: Direction-dependent magnetic conductive AFM supplied evidence against a purely interfacial interpretation in one 2025 geometry. General decomposition across contacts and molecular families remains open.
why: Identifies which chemical modifications affect spin transport and which affect injection.
key_works: J. A. Albro et al. (2025), *Measurement Platform to Probe the Mechanism of Chiral-Induced Spin Selectivity through Direction-Dependent Magnetic Conductive Atomic Force Microscopy*, [DOI:10.1021/acsnano.5c04980](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsnano.5c04980).

title: Predicting escape from bound singlet-fission triplet pairs
open: Predict absolute rates for a correlated triplet pair to separate, recombine or undergo spin conversion from molecular packing and temperature, without fitting each film independently.
status: In anthradithiophene films, a 2025 study found intersystem crossing outcompeting pair separation below 270 K. Efficient pair formation therefore does not establish efficient free-triplet production.
why: Converts excitation multiplication into extractable charge-generating excitations.
key_works: E. M. Bu Ali et al. (2025), *Intersystem Crossing Outcompetes Triplet-Pair Separation from 1(TT) below 270 K in Anthradithiophene Films*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c00001](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c00001).

title: Absolute free-triplet yields distinct from correlated pairs
open: Calibrate separate counts of strongly bound pairs, weakly coupled pairs and free triplets throughout a singlet-fission film.
status: Optical and spin measurements distinguish states in selected systems, but overlapping signatures and newly resolved intersystem-crossing and quintet channels complicate absolute yields.
why: Makes reported singlet-fission yields comparable across materials and laboratories.
key_works: Bu Ali et al. (2025), *Intersystem Crossing Outcompetes Triplet-Pair Separation from 1(TT) below 270 K in Anthradithiophene Films*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c00001](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c00001); J. Grüne et al. (2026), *High-spin state dynamics and quintet-mediated emission in intramolecular singlet fission*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-67383-3](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-67383-3).

title: Bright, stable emitters with inverted singlet–triplet gaps
open: Realize inverted-gap molecules combining appreciable oscillator strength, rapid triplet harvesting and operational device stability, with experimentally verified excited-state ordering.
status: Inverted-gap examples exist. A 2026 search screened 118,081 aza-hydrocarbons and proposed 34 candidates with oscillator strengths at least 0.01; their combined predicted advantages require experimental realization.
why: Could reduce exciton residence times and OLED efficiency losses.
key_works: R. Mahaan and Z. Shuai (2026), *Cost-Effective Digital Discovery of Aza-Hydrocarbons via Isomerization for Inverted Singlet–Triplet Emitters*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c01031](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.6c01031).

title: Predicting reverse intersystem-crossing rates without fitted kinetics
open: Calculate absolute reverse intersystem-crossing rates across TADF environments, including higher triplets, conformational motion and vibronic coupling, while predicting isotope and temperature effects consistently.
status: Isotopologue and magnetic-response experiments identified spin–orbit-dominated crossing in studied cyanoarenes in 2025–2026. Transferable quantitative rates remain harder than gap prediction.
why: Connects chemical modifications to delayed-fluorescence speed and losses.
key_works: A. Morgenstern et al. (2026; online 2025), *Unlocking Spin Dynamics: Spin-Orbit Coupling Driven Spin State Interconversion in Carbazole-Containing TADF Emitters*, [DOI:10.1002/adom.202501504](https://doi.org/10.1002/adom.202501504).

title: Predicting molecular spin coherence independently of magnetic relaxation
open: Predict longitudinal relaxation and phase-coherence times from molecular and crystal structures, separating phonon, nuclear-spin and pure-dephasing contributions.
status: Lunghi’s 2026 calculation predicts seconds-scale relaxation at 77 K but sub-10-ns coherence in a studied molecule. Experimental validation and transferable design rules remain open.
why: Identifies molecular magnets suitable for coherent quantum operations.
key_works: A. Lunghi (2026), *A unified ab initio theory of spin-phonon relaxation and decoherence uncovers fast dephasing in magnetic molecules*, [DOI:10.1126/sciadv.aeb3868](https://doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aeb3868).

title: Error-controlled PCET in the intermediate electron–phonon regime
open: Obtain controlled photoinduced proton-coupled electron-transfer rates between weak-coupling and fully polaronic limits, including solvent memory, tunneling and kinetic-isotope effects.
status: A 2026 variational-polaron treatment bridges standard limiting descriptions. Its interpolation does not supply general error bounds for realistic intermediate-coupling reactions.
why: Predicts when donor, solvent or vibrational changes accelerate coupled charge transfer.
key_works: C. Venkataraman (2026), *The variational polaron formalism for photoinduced proton-coupled electron transfer*, [DOI:10.1063/5.0324969](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0324969).

title: Distance laws and pathway competition in proton-coupled energy transfer
open: Measure separate dependences on energy-donor separation, proton-transfer distance and vibronic resonance, identifying when concerted proton-coupled energy transfer defeats competing sequential pathways.
status: PCEnT was demonstrated in 2022. A 2025 triad calculation supplies microscopic rates; broadly tested distance and competition laws remain undeveloped.
why: Enables proton motion to control excitation routing without net electron transfer.
key_works: B. Pettersson Rimgard et al. (2022), *Proton-Coupled Energy Transfer in Molecular Triads*, [DOI:10.1126/science.abq5173](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.abq5173); K. Cui and S. Hammes-Schiffer (2025), *Theoretical Insight into Proton-Coupled Energy Transfer in an Anthracene-Phenol-Pyridine Triad*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c03866](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c03866).

title: Directly resolving the charge-density oscillation of correlation-driven migration
open: Resolve coherent electronic-density oscillations after selective ionization while excluding nuclear motion and incoherent populations as explanations.
status: Correlation-driven adenine signatures were reported in 2021. A 2025 study still identified direct observation of the predicted quantum beating as elusive and proposed infrared preparation with X-ray probing.
why: Tests whether correlation moves chemically meaningful charge before nuclei respond.
key_works: E. P. Månsson et al. (2021), *Real-time observation of a correlation-driven sub 3 fs charge migration in ionised adenine*, [DOI:10.1038/s42004-021-00510-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s42004-021-00510-5); C. Guiot du Doignon et al. (2025), *Correlation-driven charge migration triggered by infrared multi-photon ionization*, [DOI:10.1039/D5SC02374B](https://doi.org/10.1039/D5SC02374B).

title: Causal product control by the initial electronic coherence
open: Demonstrate that changing an initial electronic relative phase, at fixed populations and deposited energy, changes a later product distribution.
status: Full-dimensional ethylene simulations in 2025 predict altered nuclear motion despite rapid electronic decoherence. The controlled experimental phase-to-product test remains open.
why: Establishes whether attosecond coherent control can deliver chemical selectivity.
key_works: L. Fransén et al. (2025), *Attochemical Control of Nuclear Motion despite Fast Electronic Decoherence*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c01895](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jpclett.5c01895).

title: Quantum nuclear dynamics with nonequilibrium electronic memory
open: Predict reaction rates when tunneling nuclei interact with driven electrons whose force correlations retain memory, treating quantum nuclei and colored electronic noise consistently.
status: Electronic-memory effects changed calculated hydrogen diffusion in 2025. A September 2026 preprint develops a general nonequilibrium framework; controlled quantum reaction dynamics remain a further challenge.
why: Improves reaction predictions for molecular junctions and electronically driven surfaces.
key_works: G. Trenins and M. Rossi (2025), *Non-Markovian Effects in Quantum Rate Calculations of Hydrogen Diffusion with Electronic Friction*, [DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.226201](https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.226201); S. L. Rudge et al. (2026), *A General Non-Markovian Electronic Friction and Langevin Dynamics Framework for Nonequilibrium Systems*, [arXiv:2609.31254](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31254).

title: Quantitatively validated spin–vibronic dynamics with momentum conservation
open: Predict spin-changing branching and angular-momentum transfer with scalable dynamics conserving combined electronic and nuclear momenta, validated against converged quantum calculations.
status: Wu et al. showed in 2024 that conventional surface hopping can violate momentum conservation and developed constrained alternatives. Broad quantitative validation for realistic spin–orbit reactions remains incomplete.
why: Makes computed spin conversion and spin-to-mechanical motion physically consistent.
key_works: Y. Wu, J. Rawlinson, R. G. Littlejohn and J. E. Subotnik (2024), *Linear and angular momentum conservation in surface hopping methods*, [DOI:10.1063/5.0179599](https://doi.org/10.1063/5.0179599).

title: The ultracold sticky-collision lifetime puzzle
open: Explain measured molecular-complex lifetimes and loss probabilities with one microscopic account of short-range dynamics, return to reactants and external perturbations.
status: Statistical lifetime predictions remain inconsistent with observations in important regimes. Xu and Bohn’s 2026 analysis investigates their limits without supplying a universal resolution.
why: Determines whether nominally nonreactive molecules can form stable ultracold gases.
key_works: K. B. Xu and J. L. Bohn (2026), *Limits of Statistical Models of Ultracold Complex Lifetimes*, [arXiv:2604.12063](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.12063).

title: Nuclear-spin-changing branching in ultracold chemistry
open: Predict absolute probabilities for conversion of nuclear hyperfine energy into molecular rotation, including complex dynamics and magnetic-field dependence.
status: Hyperfine-to-rotational transfer was observed in Rb–KRb collisions in 2025. Predictive branching across other channels, fields and complexes remains unresolved.
why: Explains unexpected heating and losses in spin-prepared molecular gases.
key_works: Y.-X. Liu et al. (2025), *Hyperfine-to-rotational energy transfer in ultracold atom–molecule collisions of Rb and KRb*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01778-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01778-z).

title: Detecting long-range complex states as a source of dark losses
open: Observe weakly short-range-coupled collision states and measure their binding energies, lifetimes and optical responses separately from statistical short-range complexes.
status: Croft, Kendrick and Hutson’s 2026 calculations identify candidate long-range Rb–KRb states. Their connection to persistent complexes or losses surviving removal of trap light remains a hypothesis.
why: Tests a distinct mechanism for anomalous ultracold losses.
key_works: J. F. E. Croft, B. K. Kendrick and J. M. Hutson (2026), *Long-range states in collisions of ultracold molecules*, [arXiv:2604.27623](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.27623).

title: The molecular-size limit of modular optical cycling
open: Determine whether an optical cycling center remains isolated as attached molecules acquire dense vibrational manifolds, and establish achievable photon budgets with practical repumping.
status: Lao et al. retained favorable principal branching in hydrocarbon structures exceeding 30 atoms in 2025–2026. Sustained cycling at much larger size remains unestablished.
why: Extends laser cooling toward chemically complex functional molecules.
key_works: G. Lao et al. (2026; online 2025), *Bottom-up approach to making larger hydrocarbon molecules capable of optical cycling*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-025-01965-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-025-01965-y).

title: Complete accounting of weak vibrational leakage in optical cycling
open: Measure every decay branch capable of limiting a specified photon budget, including intensity borrowed through anharmonic and vibronic mixing. Million-photon cycling makes unrepumped probabilities near \(10^{-6}\) consequential.
status: Sensitive SrOH spectroscopy identified additional repumping transitions and improved trapping in 2026. The complete weak-branch tail remains difficult to predict and measure.
why: Enables reliable repumping designs for larger polyatomic molecules.
key_works: A. Lunstad et al. (2026), *High-sensitivity molecular spectroscopy of SrOH using magneto-optical trapping*, [DOI:10.1103/lrc8-566t](https://doi.org/10.1103/lrc8-566t).

title: A systematic-error-resistant polyatomic electron-EDM measurement
open: Combine long coherence, internal reversals and calibrated field sensitivity in a competitive polyatomic electron-electric-dipole-moment experiment, with matching theoretical uncertainty.
status: YbOH clock transitions with strongly suppressed field sensitivity were engineered in 2025–2026. This enables, but does not complete, the precision EDM experiment.
why: Uses molecular structure to test time-reversal-violating interactions.
key_works: Y. Takahashi et al. (2026), *Engineered Molecular Clock Transitions for Precision Measurements*, [DOI:10.1103/4t7q-d58r](https://doi.org/10.1103/4t7q-d58r); [arXiv:2508.06787](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06787).

title: Equimolar oxidative cross-Kolbe coupling
open: Selectively couple two different free aliphatic carboxylic acids at approximately equimolar loading by oxidative decarboxylation, without converting either into an activated ester.
status: Reductive heterocoupling through activated esters is established. The 2023 waveform-controlled oxidative method broadened direct scope without establishing general nonstatistical cross-coupling of similar acids.
why: Makes abundant acids interchangeable coupling partners with less activation waste.
key_works: B. Zhang et al. (2022), *Ni-electrocatalytic Csp3–Csp3 doubly decarboxylative coupling*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-022-04691-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-022-04691-4); Y. Hioki et al. (2023), *Overcoming the limitations of Kolbe coupling with waveform-controlled electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adf4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf4762).

title: Direct observation of waveform-controlled Kolbe branching
open: Measure interfacial pH, radical populations and radical-to-carbocation conversion within individual polarity cycles, quantitatively explaining dimerization, substitution and overoxidation.
status: The 2023 waveform study proposed local-pH effects. Cycle-resolved intermediate and product balances remain the experimental test of that mechanism.
why: Makes waveform selection transferable across substrates and reactors.
key_works: Y. Hioki et al. (2023), *Overcoming the limitations of Kolbe coupling with waveform-controlled electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1126/science.adf4762](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.adf4762).

title: Enantioselective capture of unbound electrogenerated carbocations
open: Trap directly electrogenerated, non-catalyst-bound tertiary carbocations with predictable enantioselectivity before rearrangement or solvent capture, without covalently attached chiral auxiliaries.
status: A 2024 method controls chiral α-imino carbocations using primary-amine catalysis. Freely diffusing tertiary carbocations present a distinct unresolved selectivity problem.
why: Enables asymmetric substitutions at crowded carbon centers from oxidizable feedstocks.
key_works: Q. Lin et al. (2024), *Enantioselective SN1-type reaction via electrochemically generated chiral α-Imino carbocation intermediate*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-024-50945-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-024-50945-2).

title: Quantitative stereoselection by chiral supporting electrolytes
open: Predict enantioselectivity from potential, ion pairing, electrolyte composition and interfacial chiral-counterion concentration across substrates and electrode materials.
status: Mao et al. demonstrated phosphine dynamic kinetic resolution with substoichiometric chiral phosphate electrolytes in 2025. Predictive generalization from the proposed interfacial mechanism remains open.
why: Makes electrolytes rationally designable asymmetric catalysts.
key_works: K. Mao et al. (2025), *Dynamic kinetic resolution of phosphines with chiral supporting electrolytes*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-025-09238-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-025-09238-x).

title: Predicting alternating-current selectivity in nonlinear reaction networks
open: Predict waveform-dependent products in networks containing radical termination, catalyst aggregation and evolving electrode coverage from independently measured kinetics.
status: Poh et al. introduced a Floquet treatment with transport in 2026. Validated predictions for nonlinear networks that lack a fixed periodic chemical environment remain a further target.
why: Reduces empirical frequency–amplitude screening.
key_works: Y. R. Poh, S. Sreekumar, L. Luo and J. Yuen-Zhou (2026), *Floquet States of Chemoselective Alternating Current Electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.6c02569](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.6c02569).

title: Preserving electrochemical waveform selectivity during scale transfer
open: Preserve local potential histories and diffusion-layer composition when transferring selective waveforms from laboratory cells to larger flow electrodes.
status: A 2026 micro-gap Kolbe reactor reported 30% higher current density from its serpentine flow field and 91.3% lower energy use than its batch comparator. General waveform-preserving scale rules remain unestablished.
why: Prevents scale-dependent changes in chemical selectivity.
key_works: L. Cong et al. (2026), *Enhanced mass transfer and kinetics for the Kolbe electrosynthesis of dimethyl sebacate via a micro-gap flow reactor*, [DOI:10.1016/j.ces.2025.123056](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ces.2025.123056).

title: Address-selective hydrocarboxylation of internal alkenes
open: Add CO₂ and hydrogen across either chosen carbon of an unactivated internal alkene while retaining the original double-bond position as the reaction site.
status: Alternating-polarity hydrocarboxylation and migratory carboxylation advanced in 2025–2026. Those methods leave independently selectable, nonmigratory internal-alkene regiochemistry unresolved.
why: Converts inexpensive internal olefins into specific acid building blocks.
key_works: Fors, Yap and Malapit (2025), *Effect of Alternating Polarity in Electrochemical Olefin Hydrocarboxylation*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202424865](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202424865); M. Dong et al. (2026), *Electrocatalytic Migratory Carboxylation of Unactivated Olefins or Halides with CO2*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202518160](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202518160).

title: Closing the nickel inventory during cross-electrophile electrosynthesis
open: Account for soluble nickel, aggregates, electrode deposits and short-lived organonickel species during aryl–alkyl coupling, linking each inventory to productive and side-reaction flux.
status: Operando monoaryl/bisaryl Ni(II) speciation was resolved for reductive biaryl synthesis in 2025. Complete accounting in aryl–alkyl networks remains open.
why: Identifies whether yield loss originates in catalyst state, deposition or radical fate.
key_works: B. T. Punchihewa et al. (2025), *Operando Analysis of Nickel Catalyst Speciation in Reductive Biaryl Synthesis Using Thin Layer Electrochemistry and a Microelectrode*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c12909](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c12909).

title: Feedback prevention of nickel-catalyst deactivation
open: Use operando catalyst-state measurements to adjust potential, ligand supply or feed before nickel leaves the productive cycle, conserving catalyst over repeated residence times.
status: A 2018 coupling study observed batch deactivation after roughly three hours and developed flow conditions. Newer speciation methods motivate this still-unestablished feedback-control target.
why: Makes fragile electrosynthetic reactions reproducible over extended production.
key_works: H. Li et al. (2018), *Ni-Catalyzed Electrochemical Decarboxylative C–C Couplings in Batch and Continuous Flow*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.orglett.8b00070](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.orglett.8b00070); Punchihewa et al. (2025), [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c12909](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c12909).

title: Closed-inventory quinone-mediated hydrogen anodes
open: Recycle quinone mediator and hydrogenation catalyst while closing their mass balances and quantifying cumulative poisoning, crossover and cathodic-product contamination.
status: A quinone-mediated nonaqueous hydrogen anode enabled hectogram pharmaceutical synthesis in recirculating flow in 2023. Sustained inventory closure across repeated production cycles remains a proposed engineering target.
why: Avoids replacing sacrificial-metal waste with a consumable mediator stream.
key_works: J. Twilton et al. (2023), *Quinone-mediated hydrogen anode for non-aqueous reductive electrosynthesis*, [DOI:10.1038/s41586-023-06534-2](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06534-2).

title: A closed phosphorus cycle for electrochemical Appel chemistry
open: Integrate alcohol halogenation or etherification with phosphine-oxide regeneration so the phosphorus reagent turns over catalytically without destroying substrates or products.
status: Halide-coupled electrochemical phosphine oxidation was demonstrated in 2025 with stoichiometric phosphorus. The 2026 tailored-oxide reduction supplies a regeneration concept, not an integrated Appel cycle.
why: Preserves useful substitution chemistry while removing oxide waste.
key_works: E. A. Hale, V. T. C. Ngo and Q. Zhu (2025), *Electrochemical Halogenation and Etherification of Alcohols Enabled by a Halide-Coupled Phosphine Oxidation*, [DOI:10.1021/acsorginorgau.5c00091](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsorginorgau.5c00091); Laverny et al. (2026), [DOI:10.1016/j.chempr.2026.102946](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chempr.2026.102946).

title: Durable halide-free propylene epoxidation with abundant metals
open: Combine high propylene-oxide-only selectivity, concentrated recovery and sustained operation in a nonhalogenated aqueous electrolyser using abundant metals.
status: A 2026 cobalt catalyst reached 40% Faradaic efficiency for oxide plus glycol over 24 hours. In–PtPdOₓ subsequently achieved 66% oxide efficiency at 70 mA/cm² and a 46 wt% stream; abundant-metal parity with long durability remains open.
why: Electrifies a major intermediate without chloride-based chemistry.
key_works: K. Koner et al. (2026), *Direct electrochemical propylene epoxidation over amorphized perovskite oxide in non-halogenated aqueous electrolyte*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01535-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01535-6); Y. Liang et al. (2026), *Electrified direct epoxidation of light hydrocarbons using alkene-binding atomic sites*, [DOI:10.1038/s44160-026-01104-6](https://doi.org/10.1038/s44160-026-01104-6).

title: Durable solid redox reservoirs for decoupled organic electrolysis
open: Repeatedly store and release charge while separating organic oxidation from its counter-reaction, without capacity loss or reactive-impurity transfer across changing feeds.
status: Decoupled charge–discharge organic oxidation and hydrogen evolution were demonstrated in 2026. Durable operation with diverse organic feeds is a remaining systems target.
why: Allows each half-reaction to operate under independently favorable conditions.
key_works: Y. Huang et al. (2026), *Decoupling charge–discharge electrolysis for hydrogen evolution and organic oxidation reactions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-71016-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71016-8).

title: Environment-dependent lifetimes of class-II atropisomers
open: Predict racemization half-lives across solvent, protonation, temperature and aggregation conditions with calibrated uncertainty, especially near practical stability boundaries.
status: A 2026 workflow correctly classified over 90% of 65 molecules containing 68 relevant torsions. Condition-dependent lifetime prediction remains more demanding than broad class assignment.
why: Enables rational handling of compounds that racemize during processing or assays.
key_works: T. Balduf et al. (2026), *Prediction of Atropisomerism for Drug-like Molecules*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.jcim.5c02720](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.jcim.5c02720).

title: Atropisomer exchange during nucleation of large drug-like molecules
open: Determine when atropisomer exchange blocks nucleation or selects a solid form, and predict crystallization while explicitly coupling exchange and nucleation kinetics.
status: A 2025 ACBI1/BI201335 comparison found barriers near 23.4 and 19.8 kcal/mol. It supports an atropisomerism hypothesis without establishing a general causal crystallization theory.
why: Improves isolation of flexible compounds whose stereochemical populations evolve during crystallization.
key_works: N. A. Stamos et al. (2025), *Beyond Barriers, Big Crystallization Hurdles: Atropisomerism in Beyond Rule of Five Compounds Explored by Computational and NMR Studies*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.5c00204](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.molpharmaceut.5c00204).

title: C–B axial chirality that survives Lewis-base coordination
open: Design axially chiral boron Lewis acids retaining configuration through repeated donor association and dissociation without sacrificing Lewis acidity.
status: Doan et al. showed in 2025 that Lewis-base binding can accelerate triarylborane atropisomerization from decades to minutes. Stability of the free borane therefore leaves catalytic-cycle stability unresolved.
why: Makes C–B atropisomers persistent asymmetric Lewis-acid catalysts.
key_works: T.-H. Doan et al. (2025), *Atropisomerism in Triarylboranes: Lewis Base Assisted Rotation at C−B Stereogenic Axis in Asymmetrical Boron Lewis Acids*, [DOI:10.1002/ange.202421931](https://doi.org/10.1002/ange.202421931).

title: Full interconversion networks of pyramidalized N–N atropisomers
open: Resolve how N–N rotation, nitrogen inversion and protonation jointly interconvert stereoisomers, identifying conditions preserving an axis across coordination changes.
status: Thermally stable N–N atropisomers with nitrogen approximately 20° out of planarity were prepared in 2026. Complete exchange networks across chemical states remain unmeasured.
why: Extends stereochemical design beyond conventional planar nitrogen axes.
key_works: H. Zhu et al. (2026), *Remote Generation of Pyramidalized N–N Axial Chirality via a Copper-Catalyzed Friedel–Crafts Reaction*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.orglett.6c03439](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.orglett.6c03439).

title: Independently programming four stereogenic axes
open: Access every distinct configuration of a four-axis molecule from common precursors, with independent control over each axis, including substrate-disfavored diastereomers.
status: Sato et al. generated up to four axes through rhodium-catalyzed cycloaddition in 2026. Independent programming of all combinations remains a further synthetic target.
why: Enables systematic tests of individual axes in molecular recognition and materials.
key_works: Y. Sato, J. Jiang, K. Yamashiro and K. Tanaka (2026), *Enantioselective Synthesis of Axially Chiral Diaryl Ethers via Rhodium-Catalyzed [2+2+2] Cycloaddition*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.3486845](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.3486845).

title: Atroposelective ether coupling without activated aromatic partners
open: Construct persistent C–O stereogenic axes from electronically unactivated aryl partners and phenols, without required SNAr activation or removable recognition handles.
status: A 2026 organocatalytic SNAr method reached 99% yield and 99% ee in its activated substrate space. General unactivated-partner coupling remains a distinct scope target.
why: Removes activation-pattern restrictions from diaryl-ether targets.
key_works: Y. Guo et al. (2026), *Atroposelective organocatalytic nucleophilic aromatic substitution for C–O bond construction*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01522-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01522-x).

title: Direct asymmetric NH transfer to dialkyl sulfoxides
open: Convert racemic dialkyl sulfoxides directly into enantioenriched unprotected NH-sulfoximines through catalytic NH transfer and simultaneous racemization.
status: Fan et al.’s 2025 iron/photoredox resolution performs well for many aryl–alkyl sulfoxides. The tested dialkyl substrate gave 29% yield and racemic product.
why: Provides compact sulfur stereocenters without chiral starting materials.
key_works: F.-X. Fan, H. Xu, S.-X. Tang, Y. Dang and F. Wang (2025), *Iron-catalysed stereoselective NH transfer enables dynamic kinetic resolution of sulfoxides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4).

title: The dark racemization pathway in iron-catalyzed sulfoxide imidation
open: Identify the nonphotochemical racemization pathway in the iron/aminating-reagent system, distinguishing electron transfer, sulfur substitution and iron–aminyl chemistry, including the base’s role.
status: Dark racemization requiring iron, ligand and aminating reagent was observed in 2025. The additional pathway and base contribution remained unresolved.
why: Could enable simpler dynamic resolutions and suppress stereochemical erosion.
key_works: F.-X. Fan et al. (2025), *Iron-catalysed stereoselective NH transfer enables dynamic kinetic resolution of sulfoxides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-56860-4).

title: Independent functionalization of the two imino nitrogens of sulfondiimines
open: Install two different substituents selectively on initially equivalent imino nitrogens while independently selecting and preserving sulfur configuration.
status: Complementary peptide and cinchona catalysts enabled enantioselective trifluoroacetylation in 2026. Diverse sequential N-functionalization with selectable configuration remains a broader target.
why: Opens sulfondiimine structures beyond narrow derivatization sequences.
key_works: E. Gaster et al. (2026), *Assessment of Complementary Catalysts in an Uncharted Enantioselective Reaction of Sulfondiimines*, [DOI:10.1021/jacs.5c23100](https://doi.org/10.1021/jacs.5c23100).

title: Scale-independent stereofidelity in sulfondiimidoyl fluoride preparation
open: Preserve configuration during scale-up by quantitatively controlling water, mixing, fluoride, alkoxide and scavenger exposure.
status: Jersovs et al. obtained highly enantioenriched products in 2026, but a fluoride-scavenger improvement failed on larger scale; alkoxide-triggered racemization was also identified.
why: Makes unusual sulfur(VI) building blocks reliably manufacturable.
key_works: G. Jersovs et al. (2026), *Stereospecific SuFEx reactivity of highly enantioenriched sulfondiimidoyl fluorides*, [DOI:10.1039/D6QO00230G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6QO00230G).

title: Stereospecific unactivated-alkyl transfer to sulfondiimidoyl fluorides
open: Replace fluoride at stereogenic sulfondiimidoyl sulfur with ordinary primary or secondary alkyl groups while preserving predictable chirality transfer.
status: The 2026 triorganozincate chemistry achieves selective allyl and benzyl transfer with complete chirality transfer. Unactivated alkyl donors remain the narrower extension target.
why: Connects modular sulfur(VI) fluorides to a wider carbon-substituent range.
key_works: G. Jersovs et al. (2026), *Stereospecific SuFEx reactivity of highly enantioenriched sulfondiimidoyl fluorides*, [DOI:10.1039/D6QO00230G](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6QO00230G).

title: Sitewise stereochemical error maps for phosphorothioate oligonucleotides
open: Identify and quantify incorrect phosphorus configurations at every linkage in long stereodefined oligonucleotides, including low-abundance combinations of errors.
status: Bis(amidine) catalysts enabled stereoselective P(V) chemistry and both solid-phase synthesis directions in 2026. Site-resolved Rp/Sp error quantification remains a separate analytical target.
why: Makes stereochemical purity claims comparable and links specific errors to function.
key_works: S.-S. Fang et al. (2026), *Multifunctional chiral bis(amidine) organocatalysts enable stereoselective synthesis of phosphorothioate oligonucleotides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41929-026-01557-0](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41929-026-01557-0).

title: Identifying the resting state in phosphine-catalyzed sulfinamide synthesis
open: Determine catalyst resting states and productive flux in the Morita–Baylis–Hillman ester/sulfinylamine reaction, directly testing the proposed dual substrate/promoter role of sulfinylamine.
status: Qian et al.’s 2026 air-stable phosphine platform produces S(IV)-stereogenic sulfinamides. Its phosphonium resting-state and promoter assignments remain mechanistic proposals.
why: Explains catalyst longevity and guides extension to less reactive partners.
key_works: C. Qian et al. (2026), *Organocatalytic enantioselective synthesis of S(IV)-stereogenic sulfinamides enabled by an air-stable chiral phosphine*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-026-02095-9](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-026-02095-9).

title: Quantitative stereochemical proteome maps for sulfonimidoyl fluorides
open: Measure matched sulfur-enantiomer pairs’ residue occupancy and reaction kinetics across native proteomes while separately quantifying hydrolysis and nonspecific binding.
status: Buffer-phase stereospecific transformations and chirality-dependent protein ligation were demonstrated in 2024–2025. Quantitative proteome-wide stereochemical reactivity maps remain open.
why: Connects sulfur configuration to selective covalent recognition.
key_works: H.-S. Huang et al. (2025), *Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral Sulfonimidoyl Fluorides Facilitates Stereospecific SuFEx Click Chemistry*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.202415873](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.202415873).

title: Direct observation of the reactive mannosyl boat conformer
open: Measure the proposed B₂,₅ mannosyl oxocarbenium conformer’s population and lifetime under glycosylation conditions, connecting its consumption to stereospecific products.
status: A 2026 computational study explains α-selectivity through minor boat conformers beyond the two-conformer model. Direct transient population-to-product accounting remains open.
why: Tests whether a minor sugar-cation population controls the major product.
key_works: W. A. Remmerswaal et al. (2026), *Beyond the two-conformer model: boat conformers provide stereoselectivity in SN1-type glycosylations of manno-type donors*, [DOI:10.1039/D6SC02312F](https://doi.org/10.1039/D6SC02312F).

title: Orthogonal natural-modification patterns in defined oligosialic acids
open: Build defined α(2,8)/α(2,9) chains with independently placed natural O-acetyl and N-glycolyl groups, preserving them during temporary chain-cap removal.
status: A 2026 stop-and-go polymerase method gives defined oligosialosides using removable benzoyl or thioethyl groups, averaging 62% isolated yield per cycle. Arbitrary native modification patterns add unresolved orthogonality constraints.
why: Tests positional modification effects separately from average composition.
key_works: J. A. Fok et al. (2026), *Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of Well-Defined α(2,8)- and α(2,9)-Linked Oligosialosides*, [DOI:10.1002/anie.4872790](https://doi.org/10.1002/anie.4872790).

title: Long heparan-sulfate chains with independently programmed epimers and sulfates
open: Specify every uronate epimer and N-, 2-O-, 3-O- and 6-O-sulfation site in long chains, preserving the pattern through synthesis and purification.
status: A 2023 platform produced all 64 N-/2-O-/6-O-sulfation patterns on a fixed tetrasaccharide framework. Long-chain epimer and 3-O-sulfate programming remain outside that comprehensive library.
why: Enables causal tests of long-range sulfation domains.
key_works: L. Wang et al. (2023), *Efficient platform for synthesizing comprehensive heparan sulfate oligosaccharide libraries for decoding glycosaminoglycan–protein interactions*, [DOI:10.1038/s41557-023-01248-4](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41557-023-01248-4).

title: Complete native heparan-sulfate chain sequencing
open: Recover an individual native chain’s ordered sugars, uronate epimers and sulfation sites, retaining fragment provenance across long domains and rare 3-O-sulfated motifs.
status: The 2020 SIMMS² method used 36 synthetic di- to decasaccharide standards and sequenced natural hexasaccharides. Complete native-chain reconstruction remains beyond that fragment-level result.
why: Makes the proposed heparan-sulfate sequence code directly readable.
key_works: R. L. Miller et al. (2020), *Shotgun ion mobility mass spectrometry sequencing of heparan sulfate saccharides*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-020-15284-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-020-15284-y).

title: Unbiased quantitative inventories of heparan-sulfate 3-O-sulfation
open: Quantify native 3-O-sulfated motifs with calibrated recovery across neighboring sulfate patterns and epimers, distinguishing rarity from poor release, enrichment or ionization.
status: Cationic-peptide enrichment followed by HILIC–cyclic-ion-mobility MS improved detection in 2025. Absolute motif abundances still require recovery and selectivity corrections.
why: Enables reliable comparisons of rare but functionally important sulfation.
key_works: E. Mernie et al. (2025), *Untangling Heparan Sulfate 3-O-Sulfation Using a Novel Offline Cationic-Peptide Affinity Enrichment, Followed by HILIC-cIM-MS*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.analchem.4c05019](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.4c05019).

title: Native sialic-acid O-acetyl maps before migration
open: Recover the original C7/C8/C9 O-acetyl distribution while separately quantifying migration during quenching, extraction, digestion and analysis.
status: Reversible pH-dependent migration was established in 2021; positional and linkage assignment by ion-mobility MS followed in 2023. Preservation of the original biological distribution remains a separate requirement.
why: Prevents analytical rearrangement from masquerading as biological regulation.
key_works: Y. Ji et al. (2021), *Reversible O-Acetyl Migration within the Sialic Acid Side Chain and Its Influence on Protein Recognition*, [DOI:10.1021/acschembio.0c00998](https://doi.org/10.1021/acschembio.0c00998); G. M. Vos et al. (2023), *Sialic acid O-acetylation patterns and glycosidic linkage type determination by ion mobility-mass spectrometry*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-023-42575-x](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-023-42575-x).

title: Localizing three or more adjacent mucin O-glycans
open: Assign individual glycan compositions to three or more nearby serine/threonine residues with calibrated confidence, separating isomers having identical total composition.
status: The 2026 DeepGPO framework supports singly and doubly glycosylated peptides. Its authors identify three-plus glycans as beyond current capability because of spectral complexity and scarce training data.
why: Resolves dense site patterns defining mucin surfaces.
key_works: Y. Zong, Y. Wang and L. Qiao (2026), *Deep Learning Prediction of O-Glycopeptide Tandem Mass Spectra Enhances O-Glycoproteomics*, [DOI:10.1002/advs.76760](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.76760).

title: A synthetic ground-truth benchmark for dense O-glycosite localization
open: Create blinded, independently verified positional-isomer mixtures spanning adjacent sites, three-plus glycans and fragmentation methods, measuring false localization separately from composition identification.
status: The 2026 DeepGPO study explicitly identifies a shortage of synthetic glycopeptide datasets for independent validation. Database-assignment agreement does not establish positional ground truth.
why: Tests the specific ambiguity that O-glycoproteomics tools claim to resolve.
key_works: Y. Zong, Y. Wang and L. Qiao (2026), *Deep Learning Prediction of O-Glycopeptide Tandem Mass Spectra Enhances O-Glycoproteomics*, [DOI:10.1002/advs.76760](https://doi.org/10.1002/advs.76760).

title: Complete enzymatic release of structurally diverse O-glycans
open: Release intact mucin-type O-glycans across all eight cores and common extensions from native proteins without removing informative terminal modifications.
status: The 2025 POGases broadened release to cores 1, 2 and 3 and selected sialylated structures. Native substrates remained harder than denatured ones; combined core coverage and accessibility remain unresolved.
why: Reduces structural bias introduced before instrumental analysis.
key_works: L. Zhou et al. (2025), *Dual functional POGases from bacteria encompassing broader O-glycanase and adhesin activities*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-025-57143-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-025-57143-8).

title: Are wybutosine derivatives yW-72 and yW-86 glycoRNA attachment sites?
open: Determine whether native yW-72 and yW-86 carry covalent N-glycans and establish their bond structures, excluding indirect release or co-enrichment.
status: Xie et al. established acp³U attachment in 2024. Their experiments also recovered carboxyl-containing yW derivatives, but equivalent direct linkage proof remains missing.
why: Tests whether RNA glycosylation uses multiple attachment chemistries.
key_works: Xie et al. (2024), *The modified RNA base acp3U is an attachment site for N-glycans in glycoRNA*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044).

title: The enzyme that amidates acp³U before RNA N-glycosylation
open: Identify and reconstitute the proposed conversion of acp³U’s carboxyl group into a glycosylation-competent carboxamide, or establish an alternative linkage-forming route.
status: The 2024 acp³U study explicitly proposes an unidentified amidating enzyme upstream of oligosaccharyltransferase. Known genetic and transport dependencies do not identify that activity.
why: Closes a missing chemical step in glycoRNA biosynthesis.
key_works: Xie et al. (2024), *The modified RNA base acp3U is an attachment site for N-glycans in glycoRNA*, [DOI:10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cell.2024.07.044).

title: Native glycoRNA site occupancy and complete glycan structures
open: Jointly identify RNA sequence, modified nucleotide, intact attached glycan and site occupancy while preserving their molecular association.
status: Attachment chemistry advanced in 2024. A 2026 liver study identified altered enriched RNA populations and SIDT1/DTWD2 roles, without producing a complete sequence–site–glycan–occupancy census.
why: Makes individual glycoRNA chemical species measurable.
key_works: C. Dong et al. (2026), *Impaired glycoRNA biogenesis in metabolic-dysfunction associated steatotic liver disease*, [DOI:10.1016/j.jhep.2026.04.034](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jhep.2026.04.034).

title: Complete intact-ganglioside structural assignment
open: Determine glycan sequence and linkage, ceramide chains, every double-bond position and relevant stereochemistry on the same native molecule.
status: A 2026 HILIC–nanoESI-MS/MS workflow quantified 80 species across 18 subclasses in ten mouse tissues. Molecular-species annotation still falls short of complete stereochemical structures.
why: Distinguishes compositionally identical molecules with different membrane functions.
key_works: N. Troppmair et al. (2026), *Comprehensive Isomer-Resolved Ganglioside Profiling by HILIC-nanoESI-MS/MS*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c00380](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.6c00380).

title: Spatial maps retaining both ganglioside glycan and lipid isomer identity
open: Map tissue gangliosides with simultaneous glycan-linkage and ceramide-double-bond resolution, calibrated abundance and measured reaction-induced displacement.
status: On-tissue capture–epoxidation resolved glycosphingolipid C=C positional isomers in 2026. Simultaneous glycan-linkage resolution and validated native spatial abundance remain additional targets.
why: Links exact glycolipid structures to tissue organization.
key_works: Y. Lv et al. (2026), *Mass Spectrometry Imaging of Glycosphingolipid C═C Position Isomers by On-tissue Capture-Epoxidation on a Diselenide-Functionalized Covalent Organic Framework*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.analchem.6c00547](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.analchem.6c00547).

title: Predicting Siglec cis/trans competition from native glycan presentation
open: Predict binding to the same versus opposing membranes from glycan identity, carrier, density, mobility and geometry, including multivalent competition.
status: A 2026 atlas measured 14 functional human Siglecs against 114 glycans with arrays and cellular assays. Predictive native-presentation models remain open.
why: Explains why identical glycans can generate different recognition outcomes.
key_works: S. Leviatan Ben-Arye et al. (2026), *An atlas of human siglecs integrates expression, affinity, and cis/trans sialoglycan recognition profiles*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-71086-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-71086-8).

title: Predicting site-specific MUC1 glycoforms from Golgi organization
open: Predict joint MUC1 site occupancy and glycan structures from enzyme localization, residence times, nucleotide-sugar supply and preceding modifications.
status: A 2026 in-vitro Golgi model reproduced divergent MUC1 processing and enzyme-location effects. Quantitative cellular glycoform distributions remain beyond that controlled reconstruction.
why: Connects intracellular processing to cell-surface chemical architecture.
key_works: A. Nashed, K. Dilsook, T. Senapathi and K. J. Naidoo (2026), *An in vitro approach for simulating divergent Golgi O-glycosylation of tumor-associated MUC1 from normal MUC1*, [DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-72151-y](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-72151-y).

title: Predicting organic multilayer assembly on soil minerals
open: Predict successive organic-layer compositions on ferrihydrite, aluminium hydroxides and carbonate minerals, including arrival order, aggregation and displacement.
status: A 2024 study showed lipid/peptide adsorption enhancing subsequent carbohydrate/lignin uptake through dispersion and multilayering. Natural-mixture prediction remains open.
why: Separates durable molecular association from apparent uptake caused by changing surface area.
key_works: O. Qafoku et al. (2024), *Synergetic Effects of Soil Organic Matter Components During Interactions with Minerals*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c07380](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c07380).

title: Molecule-resolved carbon partition during ferrihydrite recrystallization
open: Predict which molecules escape, remain adsorbed or become occluded during Fe(II)-driven ferrihydrite transformation under changing redox and ligand histories.
status: A 2025 study distinguished <3, 3–10 and >10 kDa pools with different sequestration behavior. Those fractions do not provide transferable molecule-specific retention laws.
why: Identifies carbon vulnerable during iron-mineral turnover.
key_works: F. Liu et al. (2025), *Probing Molecular Level and Subnanoscale Stabilization Mechanisms of Organic Carbon Species during Fe(II)-Induced Ferrihydrite Transformation*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.5c04803](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.5c04803).

title: Ferrihydrite-radical branching between carbon polymerization and destruction
open: Quantify when oxygen-vacancy-mediated reactions polymerize organic matter versus fragment or mineralize it, closing carbon balances across redox cycles.
status: Surface polymerization of decomposed straw-derived matter was demonstrated in 2025, involving carbon-centered radicals and phenol–quinone chemistry. Competing long-term carbon fates remain unresolved.
why: Determines whether mineral radical chemistry increases net carbon storage.
key_works: Y. Huang et al. (2025), *Oxygen Vacancies on Ferrihydrite Promote Surface Polymerization of Decomposing Straw-Derived Dissolved Organic Matter: Implications for Soil Carbon Sequestration*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.5c00204](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.5c00204).

title: Direct measurement of fast-cycling mineral-bound carbon
open: Measure molecular residence-time distributions without confusing desorption, microbial consumption and replacement by newly adsorbed carbon.
status: A 2025 analysis documents mineral-associated turnover spanning minutes to years and a lack of consensus on direct quantification. Standardized molecular measurements remain missing.
why: Prevents operational soil fractions from being mistaken for kinetic pools.
key_works: A. Jilling et al. (2025), *Evidence for the existence and ecological relevance of fast-cycling mineral-associated organic matter*, [DOI:10.1038/s43247-025-02681-8](https://doi.org/10.1038/s43247-025-02681-8).

title: Separating direct ligand release from microbial mineral-carbon priming
open: Attribute rhizosphere carbon release quantitatively to mineral dissolution, competitive displacement and microbial stimulation using simultaneous mineral, molecular and isotope balances.
status: Root-exudate destabilization was demonstrated in 2015; model experiments separated oxalate, glucose and catechol effects in 2021. Intact-root attribution remains open.
why: Explains when additional plant carbon increases or decreases soil storage.
key_works: M. Keiluweit et al. (2015), *Mineral protection of soil carbon counteracted by root exudates*, [DOI:10.1038/nclimate2580](https://doi.org/10.1038/nclimate2580); H. Li et al. (2021), *Simple Plant and Microbial Exudates Destabilize Mineral-Associated Organic Matter via Multiple Pathways*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.0c04592](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.0c04592).

title: Phosphate-dependent arsenic release during iron-mineral redox cycling
open: Predict arsenate reduction, secondary-mineral incorporation and remobilization as phosphate ratios and Fe(II) supply change repeatedly.
status: A 2025 study followed transformation for 180 days, resolving phosphate-dependent green-rust persistence and arsenic partitioning. Changing groundwater histories remain insufficiently predictable.
why: Tests the permanence of iron-based arsenic immobilization.
key_works: J. P. H. Perez et al. (2025), *Coexisting Phosphate Controls Arsenate Speciation and Partitioning during Fe(II)-Catalyzed Ferrihydrite Transformation*, [DOI:10.1021/acsearthspacechem.5c00061](https://doi.org/10.1021/acsearthspacechem.5c00061).

title: Reaction-order-dependent arsenic fate during ferrihydrite sulfidation
open: Predict arsenic release and recapture when microbial iron reduction and sulfide production occur in different sequences, including subsequent reoxidation.
status: A 2025 batch study showed strong reaction-order and sulfide-concentration effects. History-dependent field kinetics remain open.
why: Prevents overgeneralization from a single anoxic immobilization pathway.
key_works: B. Zhang, J. Tong, K. Gao and C. Liu (2025), *Effect of sulfidogenesis on ferrihydrite geochemistry and associated arsenic fate*, [DOI:10.1016/j.envpol.2024.125326](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.envpol.2024.125326).

title: Maintaining arsenate selectivity in living rice-root iron plaques
open: Establish when growing and aging plaques retain arsenate preferentially over phosphate despite exudates, mineral changes and fluctuating redox while maintaining phosphorus uptake.
status: A 2026 ferrihydrite/goethite study measured preferential arsenate binding and phosphate displacement. Durable selectivity in heterogeneous living plaques remains unestablished.
why: Connects mineral chemistry to reduced contaminant entry into crops.
key_works: Y. Fan et al. (2026), *Rice Root Iron Plaque as a Molecular Sieve: Iron Oxyhydroxide-Mediated Selective Sequestration of Arsenate over Phosphate*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.5c16125](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.5c16125).

title: Predictive phosphorus release from partially oxidized vivianite
open: Predict phosphate availability during repeated vivianite oxidation, dissolution and passivation, including phosphate recapture by new iron phases.
status: A 2024 study measured sharply declining initial dissolution as oxidation increased. Coupled aging and nutrient-release predictions in soils remain open.
why: Determines whether recovered vivianite functions as fertilizer or a phosphorus sink.
key_works: R. Metz et al. (2024), *Effect of Oxidation on Vivianite Dissolution Rates and Mechanism*, [DOI:10.1021/acs.est.4c04809](https://doi.org/10.1021/acs.est.4c04809).

title: Secondary-clay passivation of basalt during enhanced weathering
open: Predict mineral-specific basalt dissolution after secondary clays form, including coating passivation and changes in reactive area under variable drainage.
status: Poor-drainage experiments in 2025 formed secondary minerals within about 20 hours and showed roughly 100-fold rate decline over 24 days. Field-grain extrapolation remains open.
why: Constrains sustained carbon removal after initial dissolution.
key_works: P. Sriwastava et al. (2025), *Experimental pathways of clay formation and kinetics of basalt alteration in poor drainage systems: Implications for weathering*, [DOI:10.1016/j.gca.2025.01.042](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.gca.2025.01.042).
